title: Temperature Streak Analyzer
spec: Write a script to analyze an array of daily temperatures. Create a function `analyze temperatures` that takes a `temperature array` and a `target threshold` integer. First, check if the `temperature array` is empty; if so, return an array of three zeros. Track the `total evaluated days` (count of days strictly greater than the threshold overall), the `current sequence length` (for contiguous days above the threshold), the `max sequence length` found so far, the `current sequence sum`, and the `best sequence sum`. Iterate through the array. When a sequence of days above the threshold ends, if the `current sequence length` is greater than the `max sequence length`, update the `max sequence length` and set the `best sequence sum` to the `current sequence sum`. Return an array of three integers: the `max sequence length`, the `best sequence sum`, and the `total evaluated days`. Include a main block that creates a test array and threshold, calls the function, and prints the result.

title: Pagination Window Calculator
spec: Write a script to calculate pagination links for a data grid. Create a function `calculate pagination` that takes three integers: the `current page number`, the `total page count`, and a `display window size`. Subtract half of the `display window size` (floored) from the `current page number` to get a tentative `first visible page`. If it is less than 1, clamp it to 1. Calculate the `last visible page` by adding the `display window size` minus 1 to the `first visible page`. If the `last visible page` exceeds the `total page count`, clamp it. Track the `left omitted count` (pages before the first visible) and `right omitted count` (pages after the last visible). Also compute a `has previous page` boolean (true if `first visible page` > 1) and a `has next page` boolean. Return an object with exactly six single-word keys: `start`, `end`, `left`, `right`, `prev`, and `next`, assigning the respective calculated variables. Include a main block calling the function with (7, 20, 5) and printing the output.

title: Physics Bouncing Ball Simulation
spec: Write a script to simulate a bouncing ball in a physics engine. Create a function `simulate bouncing ball` that takes an `initial drop height`, a `bounce restitution multiplier`, and a `minimum threshold height`. If the `bounce restitution multiplier` is out of bounds (less than 0 or >= 1), return an array of three zeros. Track the `total distance traveled`, the `current peak height`, the `total bounce count`, and the `maximum peak height` reached. While the `current peak height` is greater than the `minimum threshold height`, add the `current peak height` to the `total distance traveled` (falling). Multiply the `current peak height` by the `bounce restitution multiplier` to get the `new rebound height`. Add the `new rebound height` to the `total distance traveled` (rising), assign the `new rebound height` to the `current peak height`, and increment the `total bounce count`. Return an array containing the `total distance traveled`, `total bounce count`, and `maximum peak height`. Call the function with 10, 0.75, 1, and print the array.

title: Moving Average Filter
spec: Write a script to apply a moving average filter to numerical data. Create a function `smooth data array` that takes a `raw data array` and an integer `sliding window size`. If the `sliding window size` is even, increment it by 1. Track a `filtered result array`. Iterate through each index of the `raw data array`. For each position, calculate the `window start index` (clamped to 0) and the `window end index` (clamped to array length minus 1). Loop from the start to end indices to calculate the `current window sum`. Divide this by the number of elements in the window (the `actual window length`) to get the `local average value`. Push it into the `filtered result array`. After the main loop, calculate the `overall average value` of the entire `filtered result array`. Return an array containing the `filtered result array` and the `overall average value`. Include a main block that processes `[2, 4, 6, 8, 10]` with window size 3 and prints.

title: Order Bill Calculator
spec: Write a script to compute an order bill. Create a function `compute order bill` that takes an `item prices array`, a matching `exempt items array` of booleans, a `discount percentage rate`, and a `state tax rate`. Iterate over the prices. Track a `tax exempt subtotal` and a `taxable subtotal`. If the corresponding exempt boolean is true, add the price to the `tax exempt subtotal`, otherwise to the `taxable subtotal`. Calculate the `gross subtotal amount` by adding both. Apply the `discount percentage rate` proportionally to both subtotals to calculate the `discounted exempt amount` and `discounted taxable amount`. Apply the `state tax rate` only to the `discounted taxable amount` to get the `applicable tax amount`. The `final total price` is the sum of the two discounted amounts and the tax. Return an array: `gross subtotal amount`, `applicable tax amount`, and `final total price`. Call it with test data and print.

title: Parking Garage Fee
spec: Write a script to calculate parking fees. Create a function `calculate parking fee` taking an `entry hour number`, an `exit hour number`, a `base flat rate`, an `hourly extra rate`, and a `maximum daily cap`. Track the `adjusted exit hour`, initialized to the exit hour. If it's less than the entry hour, add 24 to the `adjusted exit hour`. Calculate the `total parked hours`. If it is zero, set it to 24. Calculate the `preliminary total fee` as the `base flat rate` plus the `hourly extra rate` multiplied by the `total parked hours`. If the `total parked hours` is greater than 12, add an `extended stay surcharge` of 10 to the `preliminary total fee`. Finally, compare the `preliminary total fee` to the `maximum daily cap`, storing the smaller value in `final approved fee`. Return the `final approved fee`. Include a main block with entry 18, exit 2, base 5, hourly 2, max 20, and print.

title: String Word Capitalizer
spec: Write a script to apply sentence formatting. Create a function `format sentence case` taking a `raw input sentence` string and an `excluded words array`. Trim leading/trailing spaces from the `raw input sentence`. If empty, return an empty string. Split the sentence into a `word tokens array`. Track a `capitalized word count`. Iterate over the tokens. Track the `current word index` and the `lowercased word version`. If the index is 0, or if the `lowercased word version` is not in the `excluded words array`, create a `capitalized word version` by uppercasing the first letter, increment the `capitalized word count`, and replace the token. Join the tokens into a `final formatted string`. If the `capitalized word count` is 0, return the string `'NONE'`. Otherwise, return the `final formatted string`. Call it with a sample sentence and print.

title: Inventory Reorder Planner
spec: Write a script to plan warehouse inventory reorders. Create a function `plan inventory reorder` taking a `current stock array`, a `minimum safe threshold`, and a `standard batch size`. Track the `total items ordered`, the `total batches required`, and the `most critical item index` (the index of the item with the largest stock deficit). Track the `largest deficit found` (initialized to 0). Iterate through the `current stock array`. If a value is below the `minimum safe threshold`, calculate the `inventory deficit amount`. If it exceeds the `largest deficit found`, update both the maximum deficit tracker and the `most critical item index`. Determine the `needed batch count` by dividing the `inventory deficit amount` by the `standard batch size` (rounded up). Calculate the `actual reorder quantity` (batches times batch size). Add these to the total trackers. Return an array of the three trackers. Run with test data and print.

title: Digital Time Converter
spec: Write a script to convert total seconds into a clock readout. Create a function `convert seconds to clock` taking an integer `total raw seconds`. Track the `total elapsed days` by dividing by 86400 (floored). Track the `remaining seconds after days` using modulo. Calculate the `full elapsed hours` by dividing this remainder by 3600 (floored). Calculate the `remaining seconds after hours` using modulo. Calculate the `full elapsed minutes` by dividing the remainder by 60 (floored). Calculate the `final leftover seconds` using modulo 60. Convert the hours, minutes, and seconds to strings, storing them in `padded hours string`, `padded minutes string`, and `padded seconds string`, adding a leading zero if below 10. Concatenate them with colons to form the `base clock string`. If `total elapsed days` is greater than 0, prepend it to form the `final clock string` (e.g., '1 days, 02:05:05'). Return the `final clock string`. Call with 90065 and print.

title: Rectangle Intersection Detection
spec: Write a script to detect screen rectangle overlaps. Create a function `check rectangle intersection` taking 8 parameters: `first rect x`, `first rect y`, `first rect width`, `first rect height`, and the corresponding 4 for a second rectangle. If any width or height is negative or zero, return 0. Calculate the `first right edge` and `first bottom edge`. Calculate the `second right edge` and `second bottom edge`. Evaluate a `has horizontal overlap` boolean by checking if `first right edge` > `second rect x` AND `first rect x` < `second right edge`. Evaluate a `has vertical overlap` boolean similarly for y-axes. If both are true, calculate the `overlap region width` (minimum of right edges minus maximum of left edges) and `overlap region height`. Calculate and return the `overlap region area`. If they do not intersect, return 0. Include a main block that tests an overlapping pair and prints the area.

title: ATM Withdrawal Dispenser
spec: Write a script to simulate an ATM cash withdrawal. Create a function `dispense atm cash` taking a `requested withdrawal amount` and an `available denominations array`. Track the `remaining withdrawal balance`, a `total bills dispensed` counter, and a `dispensed counts array`. Loop over the `available denominations array`. Calculate the `maximum fitting bills` that go into the `remaining withdrawal balance` (floored division). Cap the `maximum fitting bills` at a `maximum stack limit` of 20. Calculate the `deducted subtotal value` by multiplying the denomination by the capped count. Subtract this from the `remaining withdrawal balance`. Add the count to the `total bills dispensed` and push it to the `dispensed counts array`. If the loop finishes and the `remaining withdrawal balance` is not zero, return an array containing `[-1]`. Otherwise, return an array with `total bills dispensed` followed by the elements of the `dispensed counts array`. Call with test values and print.

title: Voting Tally System
spec: Write a script to tally election votes. Create a function `tally election votes` taking a `cast votes array` of candidate name strings. Create an `invalid votes array` containing `'NONE'` and `'VOID'`. Track a `total rejected votes` counter, the `highest vote count` seen so far, the `leading candidate name`, and create a `vote tally map` (a plain object for mapping). Iterate through the `cast votes array`. Extract the `current candidate name`. If it is included in the `invalid votes array`, increment the `total rejected votes` and continue. Otherwise, initialize or increment its count in the `vote tally map`. Retrieve the `updated candidate score`. If this score is strictly greater than the `highest vote count`, update both the `highest vote count` and the `leading candidate name`. Return an array of three elements: the `leading candidate name`, the `highest vote count`, and the `total rejected votes`. Run with a test array and print.

title: Mortgage Payment Calculator
spec: Write a script to calculate mortgage details. Create a function `calculate mortgage payment` taking the `principal loan amount`, the `annual interest rate`, and the `loan term years`. Calculate the `monthly interest rate` by dividing the annual rate by 12. Calculate the `total payment periods` by multiplying the years by 12. Calculate the `compounding multiplier factor` using `(1 + monthly interest rate) ** total payment periods`. Compute the `base monthly payment` as `principal loan amount` times `monthly interest rate` times the factor, divided by (factor - 1). Create a `formatted monthly payment` string rounded to two decimals. Calculate the `total lifetime interest` paid (`base monthly payment` times `total payment periods` minus `principal loan amount`). Return an object with strictly two single-word keys: `payment` (the formatted string) and `interest` (the `total lifetime interest` rounded to two decimals). Run with 200000, 0.05, 30 and print.

title: Sensor Data Anomaly Detector
spec: Write a script to detect anomalies in sensor data. Create a function `detect sensor anomalies` taking a `sensor readings array`, a `baseline average value`, and a `maximum allowed variance`. Track the `total anomalies detected`, the `largest deviation observed`, and a `sudden spike count`. Iterate over the readings. Extract the `current reading value`. Calculate the `absolute difference magnitude` against the `baseline average value`. If it exceeds the `maximum allowed variance`, increment the `total anomalies detected`. If it exceeds the `largest deviation observed`, update it. Additionally, if the index is >= 2, calculate a `rolling average value` of the current and previous two readings; if the `current reading value` differs from this rolling average by more than the variance, increment the `sudden spike count`. Return an array containing the three tracking variables. Call with test data and print.

title: Run-Length Encoder
spec: Write a script to perform run-length encoding. Create a function `compress string runs` taking a `raw input string`. Evaluate the `input string length`. If 0, return an empty string. Track the `current tracked character` (initialized to the first character), the `current repetition count` (initialized to 0), and the `final compressed output` string. Loop up to the `input string length`. Extract the `loop character value` at the index. If it equals the `current tracked character`, increment the `current repetition count`. If it differs, or if the `current repetition count` reaches 9 (to chunk long runs), append the `current tracked character` and the `current repetition count` to the `final compressed output`. Then, if it differed, assign the `loop character value` to the `current tracked character` and set the count to 1; if it was just a chunking reset, set the count to 0. After the loop, append any remaining character and count. Return the `final compressed output`. Run with `'aaabbbbbbbbbbc'` and print.

title: Train Fare Calculator
spec: Implement `fare(trips)` to calculate the total cost of a commuter journey. The input is an array of trips, where each trip is a two-element array containing the distance in miles as a number and a boolean flag for peak hours. The base rate for any trip is two dollars plus fifty cents per mile. If the trip occurs during peak hours, add a twenty percent surcharge to that specific trip's cost. Track the cumulative total across all trips. If the daily total exceeds fifteen dollars, cap the final result at fifteen. Return the final calculated total as a number. For example, given an array with a five mile peak trip and a ten mile off-peak trip, the output should reflect the capped daily maximum.

title: Poker Hand Evaluator
spec: Write `evaluate(cards)` to determine the strength of a five-card hand. The input is an array of five strings, each containing a value and a suit character. Parse the strings to separate values and suits. Count the frequencies of each card value to identify pairs, three of a kind, or four of a kind. Check if all suits are identical to detect a flush. Convert face cards to numeric equivalents to check if the values form a sequential straight. Return a descriptive string identifying the highest rank achieved, such as flush, straight, full house, or high card. For example, five cards of the same suit should yield the flush string.

title: Text Word Wrapper
spec: Create `format(text, width)` to break a long string into multiple lines based on a maximum line width. The inputs are a single long string and an integer maximum width. Split the text into individual words based on spaces. Iterate through the words, accumulating them into a current line buffer until adding the next word would exceed the maximum width. When the limit is reached, push the current buffer to a results array and start a new line. If a single word is longer than the width, it must occupy its own line. Return an array of formatted line strings. For example, a short sentence restricted to ten characters will split into an array of smaller string chunks.

title: Bowling Score Calculator
spec: Implement `score(rolls)` to compute the final score of a standard ten-frame bowling game. The input is an array of integers representing the number of pins knocked down on each roll. Iterate through the rolls frame by frame. Track strikes, which occur when ten pins are knocked down on the first roll of a frame, and award a bonus equal to the next two rolls. Track spares, which occur when ten pins are cleared in two rolls, and award a bonus equal to the next single roll. Accumulate the total score across exactly ten frames and return the final integer sum. For example, an array of twelve tens should return three hundred.

title: Chess Board Coordinates
spec: Design `moves(position)` to calculate all valid ending squares for a knight chess piece in a single turn. The input is a two-character string representing a starting square, utilizing files a through h and ranks one through eight. The knight moves two squares in one cardinal direction and one square orthogonally. Generate all eight mathematical destination coordinates based on these offset rules. Filter out any resulting coordinates that fall outside the eight by eight grid boundaries. Return an array of valid destination strings sorted alphabetically. For example, a starting position at the board corner will return only two valid coordinate strings.

title: Customer Loyalty Points
spec: Write `loyalty(purchases)` to calculate reward points earned from a list of transactions. The input is an array of numbers representing purchase amounts in dollars. Customers earn one point for every dollar spent over fifty dollars in a single transaction, and an additional two points for every dollar spent over one hundred dollars in that same transaction. Iterate through the list, calculating the eligible bonus points for each individual purchase. Accumulate these values and return the total integer points earned. For example, a single purchase of one hundred twenty dollars should yield ninety total points.

title: Simple Markdown Parser
spec: Implement `parse(lines)` to convert an array of plain text lines into structural HTML strings. Iterate through the input array. If a line begins with a hash symbol followed by a space, wrap the remaining text in header tags. If a line begins with an asterisk and a space, wrap it in list item tags, and ensure all sequential list items are grouped within a single surrounding unordered list tag block. Any other non-empty line should be wrapped in paragraph tags. Return a single joined string of the resulting HTML structure. For example, an input with a hash header and two asterisk items should output the matching tags combined.

title: Substring Anagram Finder
spec: Create `find(source, target)` to locate all starting indices in a long string where a substring forms an anagram of a shorter target string. The inputs are a long source string and a short target string. Calculate the character frequencies of the target string. Use a sliding window approach to traverse the source string, keeping track of the character frequencies within the current window of the same length as the target. Whenever the frequencies match exactly, record the starting index of the window. Return an array of these integer starting indices. For example, searching for a three letter word in a repeating pattern will yield multiple matching integer indices.

title: Website Breadcrumb Builder
spec: Implement `build(paths)` to generate a breadcrumb navigation trail for a website. The input is an array of URL segment strings. Start the output with a home label linked to a root slash. For each segment in the array, capitalize the first letter and replace any hyphens with spaces to create a human readable label. Construct the cumulative URL path by joining all segments up to the current one with forward slashes. Push each generated step to a results array. Return an array of two-element arrays, where each inner array contains the readable label and its corresponding full path. For example, inputs of store and new-items will produce three sequential navigation steps.

title: Sudoku Row Validator
spec: Write `verify(grid)` to check if the rows of a logic puzzle are structurally valid. The input is a nine by nine grid of integers represented as a two dimensional array. Iterate through each row and isolate the numbers one through nine. Ensure that each number appears exactly once, ignoring any zero values which represent empty spaces. If any duplicates are found within a single row, the row is invalid. Return a boolean value indicating whether all rows pass the duplication check. For example, a grid containing a row with two fives should return false, whereas a grid with unique non-zero values per row should return true.

title: Elevator Floor Scheduler
spec: Design `schedule(requests, start)` to simulate an elevator servicing multiple floor calls. The inputs are an array of requested floor integers and an initial starting floor integer. The elevator always travels to the closest requested floor first. If two requests are equidistant, it prefers to move upwards. Remove serviced floors from the pending list and accumulate the total floors traveled. Continue this process until all requests are handled. Return a two-element array containing the ordered array of visited floors and the total travel distance. For example, starting at floor five with requests for two and six will visit six first, then two.

title: Credit Card Validator
spec: Implement `validate(digits)` to verify a sequence of numbers using a modulo ten checksum algorithm. The input is an array of single-digit integers. Working from right to left, double the value of every second digit starting from the second rightmost. If this doubling results in a number strictly greater than nine, subtract nine from that product. Sum all the modified and unmodified digits together. If the final accumulated sum modulo ten equals zero, the sequence is valid. Return a boolean indicating validity. For example, a sequence designed to sum to forty will return true.

title: Time Slot Overlap
spec: Create `overlap(meetings)` to consolidate a schedule by merging overlapping appointments. The input is an array of arrays, where each inner array contains two integers representing a start time and an end time in minutes. Sort the entire schedule based on the start times. Iterate through the sorted list, checking if the start time of the current appointment is less than or equal to the end time of the previously merged appointment. If it overlaps or touches, extend the end time of the previous appointment to encompass both. Otherwise, add the current appointment as a new discrete block. Return the condensed array of interval arrays.

title: Vending Machine Change
spec: Write `change(price, paid)` to calculate the coins returned by a machine after a purchase. The inputs are the item cost and the amount provided, both in integer cents. Calculate the total difference to return. Determine the breakdown of coins using quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, always utilizing the largest possible coin denomination first before moving to smaller ones. Track the quantity of each coin type dispensed. Return an array of exactly four integers representing the counts of quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies respectively. For example, a difference of forty-one cents returns one quarter, one dime, one nickel, and one penny.

title: Recipe Scaling Calculator
spec: Implement `scale(ingredients, factor)` to adjust the quantities of a recipe for different serving sizes. The inputs are an array of arrays representing the original recipe and a numeric scaling factor. Each inner array contains a string name and a numeric quantity. Iterate over the ingredients, multiplying each original quantity by the scaling factor. Check if the newly calculated quantity is a whole number. If it is, keep it as an integer, otherwise round the value to exactly two decimal places. Return a new array of arrays containing the updated numeric quantities alongside their original names.

title: IP Address Defanger
spec: Create `defang(address)` to sanitize a network address string for safe display. The input is a string representing a standard four-part network address separated by periods. First, validate that the string contains exactly four segments and that every segment consists only of numeric digits. If the input fails validation, return a string reading invalid. If valid, replace all standard periods with a string consisting of an opening bracket, a period, and a closing bracket. Return the newly formatted safety string. For example, an input with four ones separated by periods will result in the ones separated by the bracketed periods.

title: DNA Strand Compliment
spec: Design `complement(strand)` to generate the matching opposite sequence for a genetic string. The input is a string of characters representing genetic bases. Iterate through the sequence and swap every base with its biological pair: swap A with T, swap T with A, swap C with G, and swap G with C. If any unrecognized character is encountered, skip it entirely and do not include it in the result. After forming the complete paired sequence, reverse the order of the entire string to represent the proper biological orientation. Return the final reversed string.

title: File Path Normalizer
spec: Write `normalize(path)` to resolve a raw string path into its shortest absolute form. The input is a string containing forward slashes, directory names, single dots, and double dots. Split the string by the slashes. Iterate over the segments. Ignore empty segments and single dots, as they indicate the current directory. When encountering a double dot, remove the most recently added valid directory segment from your tracking stack to simulate moving up one level. Finally, join the remaining segments in the stack with forward slashes, ensuring a leading slash is prepended. Return the resolved absolute path string.

title: Email Domain Extractor
spec: Implement `extract(emails)` to determine the frequency of host platforms in a contact list. The input is an array of strings representing email addresses. For each string, locate the at-symbol and extract the domain portion that follows it. Convert this domain portion to lowercase to ensure consistency. Count the occurrences of each unique lowercase domain across the entire list. Finally, build a result structure and sort it descending based on the frequency counts. Return an array of two-element arrays, where each inner array contains the domain string and its integer count. For example, three emails from the same host will yield a count of three.

title: Palindrome Sentence Checker
spec: Create `check(sentence)` to determine if a phrase reads the same forwards and backwards. The input is a plain string. Iterate through the characters, discarding any spaces, punctuation marks, or special symbols, retaining only alphabetical letters and numerical digits. Convert all retained alphabetical letters to lowercase. Compare the characters at the beginning of the cleaned sequence with those at the end, moving progressively toward the middle. If any mirrored pair of characters fails to match, the sequence is not a palindrome. Return a boolean indicating the final result.

title: Roman Numeral Converter
spec: Design `convert(number)` to translate a modern integer into its historical symbolic equivalent. The input is an integer ranging from one to three thousand nine hundred ninety-nine. Establish the standard mappings of values to symbol strings, including subtractive combinations like four and nine. Iterate through these mappings from highest value to lowest. While the remaining integer is greater than or equal to the current mapping value, append the corresponding symbol string to a result buffer and subtract the value from the remaining integer. Return the final accumulated string. For example, an input of nine outputs the corresponding two-character subtractive string.

title: Log File Filter
spec: Write `filter(logs, level)` to extract specific diagnostic messages from system output. The inputs are an array of raw log strings and a target severity string. Each log string begins with a bracketed timestamp, followed by a space, followed by a severity level surrounded by brackets, followed by a colon and the actual message. Iterate through the array and parse each string to isolate the severity level and the message payload. If the parsed severity level exactly matches the target severity string, add the isolated message payload to a results array. Return the final array of filtered message strings.

title: Tournament Match Bracket
spec: Implement `bracket(teams)` to generate the first round matchups for a competition. The input is an array of string team names. Check the total number of participants. If the count is odd, push a string reading bye into the array to ensure an even number. Pair the first team in the list with the last team, the second team with the second to last team, and continue moving inward until all teams are assigned. Accumulate these scheduled pairings. Return an array of two-element arrays, where each inner array represents a scheduled match. For example, an input of five teams will produce three match arrays.

title: Matrix Transposer
spec: Create `transpose(grid)` to flip a two dimensional numerical layout over its main diagonal. The input is an array of arrays representing a grid of integers, where all inner arrays are of identical length. Construct a new grid where the rows of the original layout become the columns of the new layout, and the original columns become the new rows. Iterate through the row and column indices of the original grid to correctly map each integer to its transposed coordinate location. Return the newly constructed two dimensional array. For example, a two by three layout will return a three by two layout.

title: Password Strength Scorer
spec: Write `assess(password)` to evaluate the security level of a user secret. The input is a single string. Begin with a base score of zero. Increment the score by one point for each of the following criteria met: the length is at least eight characters, it contains at least one uppercase alphabetical character, it contains at least one lowercase alphabetical character, it contains at least one numerical digit, and it contains at least one non-alphanumeric special symbol. Accumulate the final tally. Return the total integer score, which will range from zero to five.

title: Water Bill Calculator
spec: Write a function `bill(usage)` that computes a monthly water bill. The input is an array of daily water usage in gallons. The monthly charge is a base fee of fifteen dollars, plus a tiered usage cost. The first thousand gallons cost two cents per gallon. The next thousand gallons cost three cents per gallon. Any usage above two thousand gallons costs five cents per gallon. Sum the total usage across all days, calculate the cost based on the tiers, and add the base fee. Return the final total cost in dollars as a number. For example, if the input is an array of thirty elements all equal to fifty, the total usage is fifteen hundred gallons, costing twenty dollars for the first tier and fifteen dollars for the second, plus the base fee, returning fifty.

title: Library Fine Calculator
spec: Write a function `assess(records)` to calculate library overdue fines. The input is an array of pairs, where each pair contains the number of days a book is overdue and an integer representing the book category: one for standard, two for reference, three for media. Fines are calculated per item: standard items are twenty cents per day, reference are fifty cents per day, and media are one dollar per day. If any item is more than thirty days overdue, its individual fine is capped at ten dollars. Sum the fines for all items and return the total fine as a number. For example, an input of pairs five and one, and thirty-five and three would result in one dollar for the first and ten dollars for the second, returning eleven.

title: Employee Shift Wage
spec: Write a function `payroll(shifts)` that calculates the total weekly wage for an employee. The input is an array of triples, where each triple contains hours worked, the hourly base rate, and a flag indicating if it was a weekend shift (one for yes, zero for no). Regular pay applies up to eight hours per shift. Any hours beyond eight in a single shift are paid at one and a half times the base rate. If the shift is on a weekend, an additional flat bonus of twenty dollars is added to that shift. Calculate the total pay across all shifts and return it. For example, a shift of ten hours at ten dollars on a weekday yields eighty for regular and thirty for overtime, returning one hundred and ten.

title: Step Tracker Stats
spec: Write a function `stats(steps)` that processes an array of daily step counts. It must calculate and return a two-element array containing the longest streak of consecutive days meeting a ten thousand step goal, and the integer average of steps on days where at least five thousand steps were taken. If no days meet the five thousand step threshold, the average should be zero. For example, given the counts twelve thousand, eleven thousand, four thousand, and fourteen thousand, the longest streak of ten thousand is two, and the valid average is the sum of twelve, eleven, and fourteen thousand divided by three, returning two and twelve thousand three hundred thirty-three.

title: Delivery Route Distance
spec: Write a function `route(points)` to calculate the total Manhattan distance of a delivery path. The input is an array of coordinate pairs representing locations on a grid. The path always starts at the origin zero zero, visits each point in the array in order, and then returns to the origin. The distance between any two points is the absolute difference of their x coordinates plus the absolute difference of their y coordinates. Calculate the sum of all segment distances and return the total distance. For example, if the input has a single point three and four, the distance from origin is seven, and returning is seven, so the function returns fourteen.

title: Typing Speed Test
spec: Write a function `score(words)` that evaluates a typing test. The input is an array of pairs, where the first element is the target word and the second element is the typed word. A typed word is correct only if it exactly matches the target word. Calculate the total number of characters in all correctly typed words. The typing speed in words per minute is this total character count divided by five, then divided by a fixed test duration of two minutes. Return a two-element array with the integer words per minute and the percentage of correctly typed words rounded to the nearest integer. For example, if four out of five words are typed correctly totaling forty characters, it returns four words per minute and eighty percent accuracy.

title: Stock Profit Analyzer
spec: Write a function `analyze(prices)` to find key metrics from a sequence of daily stock prices. The input is an array of daily prices. The function must return a two-element array containing the maximum single transaction profit and the maximum drawdown. The profit is the largest difference found by subtracting an earlier price from a later price. The drawdown is the largest difference found by subtracting a later price from an earlier price. If no profit can be made, it is zero. For example, given prices ten, twelve, eight, and fifteen, the maximum profit is seven from eight to fifteen, and the maximum drawdown is four from twelve to eight, so it returns seven and four.

title: Discount Applicator
spec: Write a function `checkout(items)` that calculates the total cost of a shopping cart after applying category specific discounts. The input is an array of pairs, where each pair is an item price and a category code (one for electronics, two for clothing, three for groceries). Groceries get no discount. Clothing gets a ten percent discount. Electronics get a twenty percent discount, but only if the item price is over one hundred dollars. Calculate the discounted price for each item, sum them up, and return the total rounded down to the nearest integer. For example, an input of fifty and two, one hundred fifty and one, and twenty and three returns forty-five plus one hundred twenty plus twenty, totaling one hundred eighty-five.

title: Cinema Seating Allocator
spec: Write a function `allocate(row, needed)` that finds a sequence of consecutive empty seats in a single movie theater row. The first parameter is an array of zeroes representing empty seats and ones representing occupied seats. The second parameter is the number of adjacent seats required. The function must scan the row and return the starting index of the first sequence of empty seats that is long enough. If no such sequence exists, return negative one. For example, if the row is one, zero, zero, one, zero, zero, zero, one and three seats are needed, the first valid block starts at index four, so the function returns four.

title: Grocery List Compiler
spec: Write a function `compile(list)` that aggregates items in a grocery list. The input is an array of pairs, where the first element is the item name as a string and the second is the integer quantity. The function must combine all entries with the same name, summing their quantities. It then should sort the unique items alphabetically by name and return a flat array where each name is immediately followed by its total quantity. For example, given an input of apple and two, banana and one, and apple and three, the function should return apple, five, banana, one.

title: Text Readability Score
spec: Write a function `readability(text)` that estimates how difficult a text is to read. The input is a single string of lowercase words separated by single spaces, with periods representing the end of sentences. Count the total number of words, the total number of characters excluding spaces and periods, and the total number of sentences. The score is calculated as five times the average characters per word, plus two times the average words per sentence. Return the score rounded to the nearest integer. For example, a text of ten words, fifty characters, and two sentences will have an average word length of five and an average sentence length of five, resulting in a score of thirty-five.

title: Movie Rating Aggregator
spec: Write a function `aggregate(ratings)` to calculate a trimmed average of audience scores. The input is an array of integer ratings from one to one hundred. If the array has fewer than three ratings, return the arithmetic average of all ratings. Otherwise, discard exactly one lowest rating and exactly one highest rating from the array, and compute the arithmetic average of the remaining ratings. Return the final average rounded down to the nearest integer. For example, given the ratings ninety, eighty, ninety-five, and seventy, the function removes seventy and ninety-five, averaging ninety and eighty to return eighty-five.

title: Solar Panel Energy Output
spec: Write a function `solar(conditions)` that estimates daily energy production for a solar array. The input is an array of triples representing hourly data: sunlight intensity from zero to ten, temperature in Celsius, and a cloud cover flag (one for cloudy, zero for clear). Base production is intensity multiplied by fifty. If the temperature exceeds thirty degrees, base production is reduced by ten percent for that hour due to heat inefficiency. If it is cloudy, the final production for that hour is halved. Sum the energy produced across all hours and return the integer total. For example, one hour with intensity eight, temp thirty-five, and cloudy yields four hundred, reduced to three hundred sixty, halved to one hundred eighty.

title: Gym Membership Fee
spec: Write a function `membership(visits)` that calculates a monthly gym bill. The input is an array of integers representing the tier of each fitness class attended by a member: one for basic, two for premium, and three for elite. The gym charges a base monthly fee of thirty dollars. Basic classes cost five dollars each, premium cost ten, and elite cost twenty. If the member attends ten or more classes in total, a fifteen percent discount is applied to the total class fees, but not to the base fee. Sum the base fee and the adjusted class fees, returning the integer total. For example, five basic classes and five premium classes cost seventy-five, discounted to sixty-three, plus thirty returns ninety-three.

title: Flight Baggage Fee
spec: Write a function `baggage(bags)` that calculates airline luggage fees. The input is an array of triples, where each triple contains the weight in kilograms, length in centimeters, and width in centimeters of a piece of luggage. The first bag is free if it weighs under twenty kilos; otherwise it incurs a flat fifty dollar overweight fee. Each additional bag costs forty dollars as a base fee, plus another fifty dollars if it exceeds twenty kilos. Moreover, if any bag has a combined length and width exceeding one hundred fifty centimeters, an oversize penalty of thirty dollars is added. Return the total fees for all bags. For example, two bags weighing twenty-five kilos each, with normal dimensions, will cost fifty for the first, and ninety for the second, totaling one hundred forty.

title: Plant Watering Schedule
spec: Write a function `irrigate(plants)` that determines how much water is needed for a greenhouse. The input is an array of triples, each representing a plant's daily requirement: base water volume in milliliters, days since last watered, and an exposure code (one for shade, two for partial sun, three for full sun). The required volume for a plant is the base volume multiplied by the days since last watered. If the plant is in full sun, the required volume increases by twenty percent. If in shade, it decreases by ten percent. Sum the required volumes for all plants, rounding down the total to the nearest integer, and return it. For example, a base of one hundred, two days ago, in full sun yields two hundred forty.

title: Video Game Level Score
spec: Write a function `evaluate(actions)` that computes a player's final score for a game level. The input is an array of pairs, where the first element is the action code (one for enemy defeated, two for item collected, three for damage taken) and the second is the associated value. Enemies grant one hundred times their value in points. Items grant fifty times their value. Damage taken subtracts twenty times the value. The level starts with a base score of five hundred. If the final score would drop below zero, it is capped at zero. Calculate and return the final score. For example, a base of five hundred, an item worth ten, and damage worth forty results in five hundred plus five hundred minus eight hundred, returning two hundred.

title: Heat Index Calculator
spec: Write a function `heat(weather)` that calculates perceived temperatures. The input is an array of pairs, where each pair contains the actual temperature in Fahrenheit and the relative humidity as a percentage. The heat index is calculated only if the temperature is eighty degrees or higher. The formula is the temperature plus twenty percent of the humidity above fifty percent. If humidity is fifty or below, or temperature is under eighty, the heat index equals the actual temperature. Return a flat array of the calculated heat indices rounded to the nearest integer. For example, eighty degrees and seventy percent humidity yields a heat index of eighty-four.

title: Book Shelf Organizer
spec: Write a function `shelve(books)` to determine the number of shelves needed for a collection of books. The input is an array of pairs, where each pair represents the thickness and height of a book in centimeters. A shelf has a maximum width of ninety centimeters and can only hold books that are less than thirty centimeters tall. Books thirty centimeters or taller must be ignored as they require special display. Accumulate the thickness of the valid books. Whenever the accumulated thickness exceeds the ninety centimeter limit, a new shelf is started with the current book. Return the total number of shelves required. For example, four valid books of twenty-five centimeters each will require two shelves.

title: Coffee Shop Roaster
spec: Write a function `roast(batches)` that calculates the final weight of roasted coffee beans. The input is an array of pairs, where each pair is the green bean weight in pounds and the roast type code (one for light, two for medium, three for dark). Light roasts lose twelve percent of their weight during roasting. Medium roasts lose fifteen percent, and dark roasts lose twenty percent. Calculate the roasted weight for each batch, sum them all together, and return the total rounded to the nearest integer. For example, one hundred pounds of light and one hundred pounds of dark will result in eighty-eight plus eighty, returning one hundred sixty-eight.

title: Ski Resort Pass Pricer
spec: Write a function `passes(skiers)` that computes the total cost for a group of ski lift tickets. The input is an array of pairs, each containing a skier's age and the number of days they will ski. The daily base rate is eighty dollars for adults. Children under twelve pay forty dollars a day, and seniors sixty-five and over pay fifty dollars a day. If a skier is skiing for three or more days, they receive a ten percent discount on their personal total. Calculate the individual cost for each skier, sum the costs, and return the final integer total. For example, a ten year old skiing four days pays one hundred sixty minus sixteen, which is one hundred forty-four.

title: Car Wash Profit
spec: Write a function `wash(services)` that calculates the net profit for a day at a car wash. The input is an array of pairs, where each pair contains a service code (one for basic wash, two for premium wash, three for detail) and the number of vehicles processed. A basic wash charges ten dollars and costs three dollars in supplies. A premium wash charges twenty and costs five in supplies. A detail charges fifty and costs fifteen in supplies. Calculate the total revenue and total supply costs across all services, subtract the costs from the revenue, and return the profit. For example, five basic washes and one detail yield a revenue of one hundred and costs of thirty, returning seventy.

title: Marathon Pace Converter
spec: Write a function `pace(times)` that converts marathon finish times into average minutes per mile. The input is an array of pairs, where each pair contains the finish time hours and minutes. A marathon is exactly twenty-six point two miles. For each runner, convert their total time into minutes, divide by twenty-six point two to find the pace, and round to the nearest whole minute. Return a flat array of these rounded paces. For example, a finish time of four hours and twenty-two minutes is two hundred sixty-two minutes, which divided by twenty-six point two gives exactly ten, so the array includes ten.

title: Music Playlist Duration
spec: Write a function `playlist(tracks)` that calculates the total playback time of a music mix in seconds. The input is an array of pairs, where each pair is the track length in seconds and a transition flag (one for crossfade, zero for gap). Each track is played in order. If a track has the crossfade flag set to one, its last five seconds overlap with the first five seconds of the next track, effectively reducing the total playlist duration by five seconds. The last track never has a crossfade applied after it. Sum the lengths and subtract the appropriate overlap time, returning the total duration. For example, three tracks of sixty seconds each with two crossfades will total one hundred seventy seconds.

title: Courier Package Stacker
spec: Write a function `stack(packages)` that determines how many loading pallets are needed for a sequence of boxes. The input is an array of box weights in kilograms. A pallet can hold a maximum of five hundred kilograms. You must load boxes onto a pallet one by one in the order they appear in the array. If adding the next box would exceed the five hundred kilogram limit, the current pallet is finalized and a new pallet is started with that box. If any single box weighs more than five hundred kilograms, it requires its own dedicated pallet. Return the total number of pallets used. For example, weights of three hundred, two hundred fifty, and four hundred require three pallets.

title: Battery Discharge Estimator
spec: Write a function `estimate(usage)` to calculate battery depletion. The input is an array of arrays representing usage periods, where each inner array contains current draw in amps and duration in minutes. Starting with a base battery capacity of 100 amp hours, calculate each period's consumed capacity by multiplying amps by the duration in hours. If the current draw exceeds 50 amps, apply a 20 percent efficiency loss factor, meaning that period consumes 1.2 times its normal capacity. Subtract each period's consumption from the remaining capacity and return the final remaining capacity, or zero if it falls below zero. For example, given [[40, 60], [60, 30]], the periods consume 40 and 36 amp hours respectively, leaving 24 amp hours.

title: Train Schedule Delays
spec: Create a function `evaluate(times)` that analyzes train punctuality. The input is an array of arrays, where each inner array contains the scheduled departure time and the actual departure time in minutes from midnight. Calculate the delay in minutes for each train by subtracting the scheduled time from the actual time. A train is considered on time if the delay is under 5 minutes, severely delayed if it is 60 minutes or more, and just delayed otherwise. Return an array of three numbers representing the counts of on time, delayed, and severely delayed trains respectively. For example, given [[600, 600], [700, 715], [800, 890]], the function should return [1, 1, 1].

title: Greenhouse Temperature Adjuster
spec: Implement `adjust(readings)` to maintain greenhouse climates. The input is an array of numbers representing hourly temperature readings in degrees. Calculate the average of the last three readings in the array to compare against a target temperature of 72 degrees. If the average is strictly above 75, return an array containing the string "cool" and the number of degrees needed to reach the target. If the average is strictly below 68, return an array with "heat" and the required degree difference. Otherwise, return an array with "maintain" and zero. For example, given [70, 78, 80, 82], the average of the last three is 80, so the output should be ["cool", 8].

title: Courier Bonus Calculator
spec: Write `calculate(deliveries)` to compute courier pay based on trip distances. The input is an array of numbers representing the distance in miles for each delivery. The base pay per delivery is 5 dollars, but if a delivery distance is strictly over 10 miles, an additional 2 dollar distance bonus applies to that trip. After calculating the total pay for all deliveries, add a 50 dollar volume bonus to the final accumulated payout if the total number of deliveries is strictly greater than 15. Return the total payout in dollars. For example, if the input array contains 16 deliveries of 5 miles each, the total is 16 times 5 plus the 50 dollar bonus, returning 130.

title: Traffic Light Timing
spec: Implement a function `optimize(cars)` to adjust green light durations. The input is an array of numbers representing the count of cars waiting at an intersection during various cycles. The baseline green light time is 30 seconds. For every full group of 5 cars waiting above a baseline threshold of 10 cars, add 5 seconds to the green light time, up to a maximum duration of 60 seconds. Calculate the adjusted green light time for each cycle, then return the average green light time across all cycles, rounded down to the nearest integer. For example, given [5, 15, 25], the adjusted times are 30, 35, and 45, resulting in an average of 36 seconds.

title: Cable Car Capacity
spec: Write a function `evaluate(groups)` to manage passenger boarding for a tourist ride. The input is an array of numbers representing the sizes of tourist groups waiting in line. A cable car can hold a maximum of 12 passengers, and groups must board together. If a group cannot completely fit into the current cable car alongside previously boarded groups, the car departs and a new empty car is brought in for that group. Iterate through the groups to determine how many cable cars are needed to transport everyone, assuming the first group always starts in an empty car. Return the total number of cable cars dispatched. For example, given [4, 5, 5, 2], the first car takes 4 and 5, while the second car takes the remaining 5 and 2, returning 2.

title: Freelance Tax Estimator
spec: Create a function `estimate(records)` to calculate estimated taxes for a freelancer. The input is an array of arrays, where each inner array contains a monthly income amount and a monthly expense amount. The net profit is calculated as the total income across all months minus the total expenses. If the net profit is strictly greater than zero, the tax is 20 percent of the profit if it falls under 50000, and 30 percent if it is 50000 or more. If the net profit is zero or negative, the tax is simply zero. Return an array of two numbers containing the net profit and the estimated tax. For example, given [[6000, 2000], [4000, 1000]], the net profit is 7000 and the tax is 1400, returning [7000, 1400].

title: Scuba Dive Planner
spec: Develop a function `plan(depths)` to calculate the required air for a diving trip. The input is an array of numbers representing the planned depth in meters for a series of dives. Each meter of depth consumes 2 units of air, and a standard safety stop required for every dive uses an additional 50 units. If the depth is strictly greater than 18 meters, it is considered a deep dive, incurring a penalty of 30 extra units of air and requiring a second safety stop that consumes another 50 units. Calculate and sum the total air required for all dives in the array. Return the total air units. For example, given depths of [10, 20], the first dive needs 70 units and the second needs 170 units, returning 240.

title: Printing Press Ink Cost
spec: Implement `compute(jobs)` to determine the cost of print jobs at a shop. The input is an array of arrays, where each inner array contains the number of color pages and the number of black and white pages for a specific print job. Black and white pages cost 5 cents each, while color pages cost 15 cents each. If a single print job contains strictly more than 100 total pages, apply a 10 percent discount to the calculated cost of that specific job. Sum the final costs of all jobs and return the total cost in dollars. For example, given [[50, 60], [10, 20]], the first job costs 10.50 minus a 1.05 discount, and the second job costs 2.50, making the final return 11.95.

title: Server Load Balancer
spec: Write a function `balance(requests)` to analyze server distribution. The input is an array of numbers representing incoming request loads. Distribute these requests sequentially across 4 available servers using a round robin approach, accumulating the total load for each server. If any server's total load strictly exceeds 1000, return the total number of overloaded servers. If no server exceeds a load of 1000, return the maximum total load handled by any single server. For example, given [300, 400, 500, 200, 800], the servers get 1100, 400, 500, and 200, so it returns 1 because exactly one server is overloaded.

title: Exam Grade Curve
spec: Create a function `curve(scores)` to adjust exam results. The input is an array of raw exam scores provided as numbers. Find the highest score in the array, and if it is strictly less than 100, calculate the point difference needed to make the highest score exactly 100. Add this point difference to all scores in the array to create a curved grade. If any curved score ends up strictly exceeding 100 due to these bonus points, cap it at 100. Return an array of the final curved scores. For example, given [80, 90, 85], the highest is 90 so the difference is 10, meaning the output should be [90, 100, 95].

title: Wi-Fi Signal Strength
spec: Implement a function `evaluate(signals)` to classify network connections. The input is an array of negative numbers representing signal strengths in decibels. Iterate through the array and count how many signals fall into three distinct categories. A signal is excellent if it is greater than or equal to negative 50, good if it is less than negative 50 but greater than or equal to negative 70, and poor if it is strictly less than negative 70. Return an array of three numbers representing the respective counts of excellent, good, and poor signals. For example, given [-45, -60, -80, -40], the function should return [2, 1, 1].

title: Laundry Cycle Chooser
spec: Write `choose(loads)` to calculate the total time required for a series of laundry loads. The input is an array of arrays, where each inner array contains a string indicating the fabric type and a number representing the load weight in pounds. Determine the base cycle time based on the fabric: cotton takes 45 minutes, synthetic takes 30 minutes, and delicate takes 20 minutes. If the weight of the load is strictly greater than 10 pounds, add an extra 15 minutes to the cycle time for that specific load. Sum the total laundry time for all loads and return the total time in minutes. For example, given [["cotton", 12], ["delicate", 5]], the first load takes 60 minutes and the second takes 20, returning 80.

title: Hotel Room Cleaner
spec: Develop a function `schedule(rooms)` to manage hotel housekeeping. The input is an array of strings representing the status of hotel rooms, which can be dirty, checkout, or occupied. A dirty room requires a standard clean taking 15 minutes, a checkout room requires a deep clean taking 30 minutes, and an occupied room is skipped taking 0 minutes. Calculate the total cleaning time required and count the total number of rooms that were actually cleaned. Return an array containing the total time in minutes followed by the number of cleaned rooms. For example, given ["dirty", "occupied", "checkout"], the function should return [45, 2].

title: Aquarium Filter Monitor
spec: Create a function `monitor(turbidity)` to track water quality in an aquarium. The input is an array of numbers representing daily turbidity levels. The filter requires changing if the turbidity level strictly exceeds 10 for three consecutive days, or if any single daily reading strictly exceeds 25. Iterate through the readings, and if either of these conditions is met during the period, immediately return the string "change". If the entire array is processed without meeting these conditions, return the string "normal". For example, given [5, 12, 14, 11, 8], there are three consecutive days over 10, so the function returns "change".

title: Drone Flight Range
spec: Implement a function `calculate(winds)` to estimate how far a drone can fly. The input is an array of numbers representing wind speeds in miles per hour for consecutive kilometers of a planned flight path. The drone starts with 100 percent battery, and under normal conditions, flying one kilometer consumes 5 percent battery. If the wind speed for a kilometer is strictly greater than 15, the drone consumes 10 percent battery for that specific kilometer. Determine how many full kilometers the drone can complete before its battery reaches exactly 10 percent or drops below it. Return the number of completed kilometers. For example, given [10, 20, 10, 20, 10], the battery drops by 5, 10, 5, 10, and 5, leaving 65 percent, so it completes 5 kilometers.

title: Typing Error Corrector
spec: Write a function `correct(words)` to fix basic capitalization in a sequence of text. The input is an array of strings representing typed words. Iterate through the array and capitalize the first letter of any word that starts with a lowercase letter if the immediately preceding word ends with a period. The first word in the array should also be capitalized if it starts with a lowercase letter. Keep track of how many words were modified during this process. Return an array containing two elements: the array of corrected words and the total count of corrections made. For example, given ["hello.", "world"], it should return [["Hello.", "World"], 2].

title: Paint Gallon Estimator
spec: Develop a function `estimate(walls)` to calculate paint requirements for a room. The input is an array of arrays, where each inner array contains two numbers representing the width and height of a wall in feet. Calculate the square footage for each wall by multiplying width and height, then find the total square footage of all walls. Every wall requires two coats of paint, meaning the total coverage needed is twice the total square footage. One gallon of paint covers exactly 400 square feet. Determine the total number of full gallons needed by dividing the coverage needed by 400 and rounding up to the nearest whole number, then return that value. For example, given [[10, 10], [20, 10]], the coverage needed is 600, so it returns 2.

title: Beehive Honey Yield
spec: Create `predict(hives)` to estimate honey production for a farm. The input is an array of numbers representing the bee population in thousands for various hives. For each hive, the base yield is 10 pounds of honey per 10 thousand bees. If a hive has a population strictly greater than 50 thousand bees, they become highly efficient, yielding 15 pounds per 10 thousand bees for that entire hive. If a hive has fewer than 20 thousand bees, it yields zero pounds. Calculate and sum the total expected honey yield across all hives, then return the total yield in pounds. For example, given [10, 30, 60], the yields are 0, 30, and 90, returning 120.

title: Campground Fee Calculator
spec: Implement a function `charge(stays)` to process campground billing. The input is an array of arrays, where each inner array contains the number of nights requested as a number, and a boolean indicating whether an electrical hookup is required. The base rate for a site is 20 dollars per night, and an electrical hookup adds an extra 5 dollars per night to that stay. If a stay is for 7 nights or longer, apply a 10 percent discount to the total cost of that specific stay. Calculate the final cost for each stay and return the sum of all revenues. For example, given [[3, false], [10, true]], the first costs 60, the second costs 250 minus 25 for a total of 225, returning 285.

title: Bumper Car Energy
spec: Write a function `simulate(impacts)` to track a bumper car's energy levels. The input is an array of numbers representing the relative speed of successive impacts. The bumper car starts with 100 units of energy, and for each impact, the energy decreases by exactly half of the impact speed. If the car's energy drops strictly below 20 units, it enters a slow mode where subsequent impacts only drain energy by a quarter of the impact speed. If the energy drops below zero at any point, it remains at zero. Return the final energy of the car after all impacts. For example, given [100, 70, 20], the first impact drains 50 leaving 50, the second drains 35 leaving 15, and the third drains 5 due to slow mode, returning 10.

title: Ice Cream Stand Profit
spec: Develop a function `calculate(data)` to analyze daily profits for an ice cream stand. The input is an array of arrays, where each inner array contains the number of cones sold and the daily high temperature in degrees. Every cone sells for 3 dollars and has a base manufacturing cost of 1 dollar. If the daily temperature strictly exceeds 90 degrees, an additional cooling cost of 50 cents per cone is added to the manufacturing cost for that day. Calculate the total profit, which is revenue minus costs, across all days in the input array. Return the total profit in dollars. For example, given [[100, 85], [100, 95]], the profit for the first day is 200, and for the second day is 150, returning 350.

title: Concert Ticket Scaler
spec: Create a function `price(purchases)` to calculate ticket revenues for a concert. The input is an array of numbers representing the days remaining until the concert at the time each ticket was purchased. The base price for a single ticket is 50 dollars. If a ticket is purchased more than 30 days in advance, an early bird discount reduces the price by 10 dollars. If it is purchased 7 days or less in advance, a last minute premium increases the price by 25 dollars. Calculate the final price for each ticket and return the total revenue generated from all purchases. For example, given [40, 15, 2], the prices are 40, 50, and 75, returning 165.

title: Workout Energy Calculator
spec: Implement `evaluate(activities)` to calculate energy expenditure from workouts. The input is an array of arrays, where each inner array contains an activity name as a string and its duration in minutes as a number. Running burns 10 calories per minute, cycling burns 8 calories per minute, and walking burns 5 calories per minute. Any activity that lasts strictly longer than 45 minutes burns an additional flat bonus of 50 calories due to endurance requirements. Calculate the calories burned for each activity and return the total calories burned overall. For example, given [["running", 30], ["walking", 60]], the first burns 300 and the second burns 300 plus 50, returning 650.

title: Office Printer Queue
spec: Write a function `process(jobs)` to manage printer paper reloads in an office. The input is an array of numbers representing the page counts of various print jobs in the queue. The printer starts with a full tray of 500 sheets of paper. Iterate through the jobs, subtracting the required pages from the printer's supply. If a single job requires more pages than are currently in the tray, the printer must be reloaded to exactly 500 sheets before printing that job. Keep a count of how many times the printer had to be reloaded, and return the total number of reloads. For example, given [300, 400, 100], the first uses 300 leaving 200, the second triggers a reload to 500 and uses 400 leaving 100, and the third uses 100, returning 1.

title: Space Probe Telemetry Analyzer
spec: A space probe sends back a list of signal strengths as numbers. The function `telemetry(signals)` analyzes this list. Discard signals below ten as noise. For the valid signals, calculate the overall average. Then, find the longest consecutive streak of signals that are at least ten percent higher than this average. Return an array of three numbers: the count of valid signals, the integer part of the average, and the length of the maximum streak. For example, given the list ten, twelve, five, twenty, twenty two, twenty four, ten, the valid signals are ten, twelve, twenty, twenty two, twenty four, ten. The average is sixteen. The streak of signals above seventeen point six is twenty, twenty two, twenty four, which is length three.

title: Stage Race Energetics
spec: A cyclist rides through a race divided into stages, given as a list of distances in kilometers. The function `pedal(stages)` computes the total energy expended and the overall time. For each stage, if the distance is less than twenty kilometers, the speed is thirty kilometers per hour and the energy cost is fifty calories per kilometer. If twenty or more, the speed drops to twenty five kilometers per hour and the cost increases to sixty five calories per kilometer due to fatigue. The function should also count how many stages were ridden at the slower speed. Return a list of three numbers: total hours taken rounded to two decimal places, total calories burned, and the slow stage count.

title: Restaurant Gratuity Splitter
spec: A restaurant pools tips and distributes them based on hours worked, with a bonus for long shifts. The function `gratuity(shifts, pool)` takes a list of hours worked by each server and the total tip pool. First, calculate the total adjusted hours: standard hours plus an extra half hour for every hour worked over six hours by a single server. Then, determine the tip value per adjusted hour. Finally, calculate each server's share by multiplying their adjusted hours by the hourly tip value, rounding down to the nearest whole number. Return a list of the integer tip amounts in the same order as the input shifts. Example: given shifts four and eight, and a pool of one hundred, adjusted hours are four and nine. Tip per hour is roughly seven point six nine. Shares are thirty and sixty nine.

title: Quarterly Interest Projection
spec: A bank customer makes a series of deposits at the start of each quarter, represented by a list of amounts. The function `project(deposits, rate)` calculates the final balance after all quarters have passed, given the annual interest rate as a decimal. Each quarter, the new deposit is added to the balance, and then the entire balance earns interest at one fourth of the annual rate. An annual maintenance fee of fifteen is deducted at the end of every fourth quarter after interest is applied. Accumulate the total maintenance fees paid over the entire period. Return a list containing the final balance truncated to an integer and the total fees paid.

title: Fertilizer Yield Estimator
spec: A farmer evaluates different plots of land, provided as a list of pairs where each pair contains the plot area in acres and the pounds of fertilizer applied. The function `harvest(plots)` estimates the total crop yield in bushels and identifies the most efficient plot. The yield for a plot is its area multiplied by forty, plus the fertilizer amount multiplied by one point five, capped at a maximum of sixty bushels per acre. Efficiency is the yield divided by the fertilizer used. Return an array with the total estimated yield across all plots rounded down, and the one based index of the most efficient plot. If multiple tie for efficiency, use the first one.

title: Wind Turbine Power Generation
spec: A wind farm generates power based on hourly wind speeds in meters per second, provided as a list. The function `generate(winds)` computes the total megawatts produced over the period. For each hour, if the wind is below four or above twenty five, the turbine produces zero megawatts to prevent damage or due to lack of wind. If the wind is between four and twelve inclusive, the power is the wind speed multiplied by zero point five. If between thirteen and twenty five inclusive, it operates at a maximum capacity of six megawatts. Also count how many hours the turbine operated at maximum capacity. Return a list of three numbers: total megawatts, shut down hours, and maximum capacity hours.

title: Solar Flare Intensity Tracker
spec: An observatory records solar flare intensities over several days, given as a list of integers. The function `flares(intensities)` analyzes the activity level. It must find the peak intensity, the total number of flares exceeding an intensity of fifty, and calculate a threat score. The threat score starts at zero and increases by the intensity value for every flare above fifty, but successive flares above fifty add a multiplier effect: the second consecutive adds double its value, the third triple, and so on. A flare of fifty or below resets the consecutive multiplier to one. Return a list with the peak intensity, high intensity count, and total threat score.

title: Highway Toll Assessor
spec: A highway toll plaza calculates fees based on vehicle size. The function `tolls(vehicles)` processes a list of vehicles, where each vehicle is a list containing its number of axles and its weight in tons. The base toll is two per axle. If the weight exceeds ten tons, a heavy surcharge of five is added. If a vehicle has more than four axles and weighs over twenty tons, it is classified as oversized and charged double the total calculated fee. Accumulate the total revenue for all vehicles and count how many were oversized. Return an array with total revenue and the oversized count.

title: Podcast Sponsor Revenue
spec: A podcaster earns sponsor money based on episode downloads. The function `sponsor(downloads, rate)` takes a list of download counts for episodes and a base rate per thousand downloads. For any episode under ten thousand downloads, the creator earns nothing. For episodes between ten thousand and fifty thousand inclusive, they earn the base rate per thousand. For episodes over fifty thousand, the first fifty thousand earn the base rate, and any downloads above that earn one and a half times the base rate. Calculate the earnings for each episode, sum them up, and round down to the nearest integer. Return the total earnings.

title: Orbital Payload Packer
spec: A space agency is packing a rocket with scientific instruments. The function `launch(items, capacity)` takes a list of item weights and the maximum weight capacity of the rocket. It iterates through the items in order, adding each to the payload if it fits within the remaining capacity. If an item is too heavy, it is skipped and left behind. The function must track the total weight loaded, the number of items successfully packed, and the number of skipped items. Return a list containing the total weight loaded, the count of packed items, and the count of skipped items.

title: Textile Mill Yarn Demand
spec: A textile mill produces various knitted patterns. The function `knit(patterns, multiplier)` receives a list of base yarn lengths required for different designs and a production multiplier. For each pattern, the total yarn needed is the base length multiplied by the multiplier. If the total for a pattern exceeds five hundred meters, it requires an industrial spool, adding a fifty meter waste allowance. Count how many industrial spools are needed, and sum the total yarn required across all patterns including waste. Additionally, find the maximum yarn length required by any single pattern after multiplication. Return a list containing the total yarn length, the industrial spool count, and the maximum single pattern length.

title: Sleep Cycle Phase Tracker
spec: A fitness tracker records a user's sleep phases as a list of durations in minutes. The phases alternate strictly between light sleep and deep sleep, starting with light sleep. The function `sleep(minutes)` calculates the total time spent in each phase. A healthy sleep cycle requires at least twenty percent of the total sleep time to be deep sleep, and the total sleep time must be at least four hundred twenty minutes. The function should return an array with three values: total light sleep minutes, total deep sleep minutes, and a one if the healthy sleep criteria are met, or a zero if they are not.

title: Maritime Cargo Routing
spec: A cargo ship travels between ports, with distances provided as a list of nautical miles. The function `voyage(legs, fuel)` determines if the ship can complete the journey with the initial fuel given in tons. The ship consumes fuel at a base rate of zero point two tons per mile. However, for any single leg longer than five hundred miles, the ship can cruise at a steady speed, reducing the consumption rate to zero point one five tons per mile for that entire leg. Deduct the fuel used for each leg. If the fuel drops below zero at any point, the ship is stranded. Return a list with a one if it finishes the route or zero if stranded, and the remaining fuel rounded down.

title: Assembly Line Quality Control
spec: A factory produces widgets in batches. The function `inspect(batches, limit)` reviews a list where each element is the number of defects found in a batch. The maximum acceptable defect limit is provided. A batch passes if its defects are less than or equal to the limit. If a batch fails, it is discarded. If three consecutive batches fail, the assembly line is immediately halted, and no further batches are processed. The function must calculate the total number of passing batches and the total defects among those passing batches. Return a list of two numbers: the count of passing batches and the sum of defects in them.

title: Marine Tank Salinity
spec: An aquarium maintains several tanks requiring specific salt concentrations. The function `salinity(tanks)` processes a list of tanks, where each tank is a list containing its water volume in liters and desired salinity in grams per liter. For each tank, calculate the required salt by multiplying volume and salinity. If the volume is over five hundred liters, a five percent efficiency loss in mixing occurs, requiring five percent more salt for that tank. Sum the total required salt across all tanks. Additionally, count how many tanks require more than one thousand grams of salt. Return an array containing the total salt rounded to the nearest whole number and the count of large salt requirements.

title: Winter Snowfall Aggregator
spec: A ski resort tracks daily snow accumulation. The function `snowfall(daily)` takes a list of daily snowfall measurements in inches. It needs to calculate the total snowfall for the season and find the longest consecutive streak of days where it snowed at least one inch. If a day has less than one inch, it does not count towards a streak. Additionally, determine the number of heavy snow days, defined as days with more than six inches. Return an array containing the total snowfall sum, the maximum streak of snow days, and the count of heavy snow days.

title: Rescue Chopper Range
spec: A search and rescue helicopter executes a series of missions. The function `rescue(missions, fuel)` accepts a list of mission flight times in minutes and an initial fuel amount in gallons. Flying consumes two gallons of fuel per minute. Using the hoist at a rescue site consumes a flat five gallons per mission. The helicopter aborts remaining missions and returns to base if the required fuel for the next mission exceeds its current tank. It must always retain a twenty gallon reserve. The function should return an array with the number of completed missions and the final remaining fuel.

title: Highway Speed Enforcement
spec: A traffic camera records passing vehicle speeds. The function `enforce(speeds, limit)` evaluates a list of speeds against a posted speed limit. Vehicles going at or below the limit are ignored.
