spec: The entry point `monitor(sections, consumption)`. The sections input is a list of cave segments containing length and airflow. The consumption is the oxygen usage rate of the team per hour. For each segment, calculate the transit time by dividing the length by a walking speed of 400 meters per hour. The available oxygen in a segment is proportional to its airflow multiplied by 10. If the available oxygen is less than the team consumption for that transit time, the segment is considered an anoxic hazard. Accumulate the total transit time and count the number of hazard segments. Return a list containing the total transit time in hours and the hazard count.

title: Optical Prism Dispersion
spec: The entry point `refract(angles, index)`. The angles input is a list of incident light angles in degrees. The index is a base refractive index of the glass. For each angle, convert it to radians. Calculate the refraction angle for red light using the base index minus 0.02, and for blue light using the base index plus 0.02, applying the sine ratio where the outside medium is 1. The separation angle is the absolute difference between the red and blue refraction angles in degrees. Determine the maximum separation angle among all incident angles and the average separation angle. Return a list with the maximum separation and the average separation rounded to three decimal places.

title: Bonsai Tree Pruning Schedule
spec: The entry point `schedule(trees, shape)`. The trees input is a list of objects containing growth and density. The shape is the target aesthetic index. For each tree, calculate the optimal pruning interval in weeks by dividing the target shape index by the product of its growth and density. If the calculated interval is less than 2 weeks, set it to 2 weeks to avoid stressing the tree. If it is greater than 12 weeks, cap it at 12 weeks. Count how many trees require pruning more frequently than every 4 weeks. Calculate the average pruning interval across all trees. Return a list with the average interval and the high-maintenance tree count.

title: Radio Telescope Signal Amplifier
spec: The entry point `amplify(signals, noise)`. The signals input is a list of faint radio frequency readings. Iterate through the signals to apply an amplification curve. If a reading is below the noise threshold, it is considered static and set to zero. If it exceeds the noise, subtract the noise, multiply the remainder by an amplification factor of 2.5, and apply a high-pass filter cap of 1000. Identify any continuous sequences of non-zero amplified signals. Calculate the total energy of the longest continuous sequence by summing its values. Return a list containing the total energy of the longest sequence and the highest single amplified signal value.

title: Snowboard Halfpipe Amplitude
spec: The entry point `estimate(runs, friction)`. The runs input is a list of initial drop-in speeds. The friction is a speed reduction multiplier between 0 and 1. For each run, the speed at the bottom of the pipe is the drop-in speed multiplied by the friction factor. As the snowboarder travels up the opposite transition wall, calculate the vertical amplitude above the lip. The amplitude is the square of the bottom speed divided by 19.6, minus a fixed wall height of 4 meters. If the result is negative, the amplitude is zero. Find the maximum amplitude achieved across all runs and count how many runs resulted in an amplitude greater than 2 meters. Return a list with the maximum amplitude and the high-air count.

title: Sourdough Starter Activity
spec: The entry point `track(volumes, time)`. The volumes input is a list of consecutive volume measurements of the starter taken at equal time intervals. The time parameter is the hours between each measurement. Find the initial volume, which is the first element in the list. For each subsequent measurement, calculate the expansion ratio by dividing the volume by the initial volume. Identify the peak ratio reached during the fermentation process and the total elapsed time from the start until this peak was first achieved. Count how many measurements showed a ratio strictly greater than 2.0. Return a list containing the peak ratio, the time to peak in hours, and the count of highly active measurements.

title: Volleyball Serve Trajectory
spec: The entry point `serve(strikes, net)`. The strikes input is a list of objects containing speed and angle. The net parameter is the height of the net in meters. For each strike, assume a starting height of 2.5 meters. Convert the angle from degrees to radians. Calculate the horizontal distance traveled when the ball reaches the net, which is 9 meters away. The time to reach the net is 9 divided by the horizontal velocity. Calculate the vertical height of the ball at this time, accounting for gravity at 9.8 meters per second squared. A serve clears the net if its height is strictly greater than the net height. Count the successful clears and find the maximum clearance margin. Return a list with the success count and maximum margin.

title: Windshield Wiper Motor
spec: The entry point `wipe(conditions, vehicle)`. The conditions input is a list of rain intensities from 1 to 10. The vehicle parameter is the speed of the car. For each rain intensity, calculate a base wipe frequency in cycles per minute by multiplying the intensity by 5. Add a speed modifier: if the vehicle speed exceeds 80, add 10 cycles; if it exceeds 120, add 20 cycles. However, the wipe frequency is mechanically limited to a maximum of 75 cycles per minute. Calculate the average wipe frequency across all given rain conditions. Also identify the longest consecutive streak of conditions that maxed out the wiper motor at 75 cycles. Return a list with the average frequency and the max out streak length.

title: Artillery Shell Trajectory
spec: The entry point `fire(shots, wind)`. The shots input is a list of objects containing velocity and elevation. The wind parameter is a headwind speed reduction. For each shot, convert the elevation from degrees to radians. The effective initial velocity is the given velocity minus the wind resistance. Calculate the horizontal and vertical components of the effective velocity. The time of flight is twice the vertical velocity divided by gravity at 9.8. The total horizontal range is the horizontal velocity multiplied by the time of flight. Determine the maximum range achieved among all shots and the highest peak altitude, which is the square of the vertical velocity divided by 19.6. Return a list with max range and peak altitude rounded to the nearest integer.

title: Origami Crease Stress
spec: Calculate the cumulative structural stress on a sheet of paper given a sequence of folds. Implement `fold(instructions)` where the parameter is a list of lists, and each inner list contains a string for the fold type, a number for the fold length, and a number for the paper layer thickness. A mountain fold adds two units of base stress, while a valley fold adds one unit. Multiply the base stress by the layer thickness to find the applied stress. If the fold length is greater than ten centimeters, add an extra penalty of five units to that applied stress. Return the total accumulated stress across the entire sequence. Example: given an input list containing one fold with mountain, twelve, and three, the output should be eleven.

title: Fencing Match Scorer
spec: Evaluate a series of exchanges to determine the final score of a match. Implement `fence(exchanges)` where the parameter is a list of lists, each containing a string for fencer one action, a string for fencer two action, and a number for the priority advantage. First determine the priority action, which is the action of the fencer whose number matches the priority advantage. A hit action awards one base point, while a parry action awards zero points. If the priority action is a riposte, it awards two points. The calculated points are only added to the score of the fencer with the priority advantage. Return a list of two numbers representing the final score for fencer one and fencer two respectively. Example: given an input list containing one exchange of riposte, hit, and one, the output should be a list containing two and zero.

title: Kite Flying Tension
spec: Determine the maximum aerodynamic tension on a string during a flying session. Implement `fly(conditions)` where the parameter is a list of lists, each representing a moment and containing wind speed, kite surface area, and tail length. The base lift is calculated by multiplying the wind speed by the surface area. The tail drag is computed by multiplying the tail length by two point five. The net tension for a given moment is the base lift minus the tail drag, with a minimum possible net tension of zero. Find the net tension for each moment and return the highest net tension recorded across the session. Example: given a moment with wind speed twelve, area three, and tail length four, the output should be twenty six.

title: Calligraphy Ink Usage
spec: Estimate the total volume of pigment required to complete a calligraphy piece. Implement `write(strokes)` where the parameter is a list of lists, each containing brush pressure, stroke length, and a string for the paper texture. The basic ink volume per stroke is determined by multiplying the brush pressure by the stroke length. If the paper texture is rough, multiply the basic volume by one point five to get the adjusted volume, otherwise the adjusted volume is the basic volume. If the brush pressure exceeds five units, a splatter penalty of two extra units is added to the adjusted volume. Calculate the final volume for each stroke and return the total sum of ink volume required. Example: given pressure six, length three, and smooth texture, the output should be twenty.

title: Tap Dance Rhythm
spec: Assess the rhythmic precision and difficulty of a dance routine. Implement `tap(beats)` where the input is a list of lists, each containing a string for step type, a number for timing gap in seconds, a number for step complexity, and a boolean indicating if a stumble occurred. A shuffle step is perfect if its timing gap is less than zero point five. A flap step is perfect if the timing gap is strictly less than zero point three. Any other step requires a gap of exactly zero point four to be perfect. If a step is perfect, multiply its step complexity by two to get the base step score; otherwise the base step score equals the step complexity. If a stumble occurred, subtract one from the base step score. Return the total accumulated score for the routine. Example: given a step with shuffle, zero point four, three, and false, the output should be six.

title: Mushroom Foraging Yield
spec: Calculate the expected harvest from various woodland locations. Implement `forage(spots)` where the parameter is a list of lists, each containing a number for humidity level, a number for oak tree count, and a number for soil acidity. The base yield is determined by multiplying the oak tree count by three. If the humidity level is above eighty, a humidity multiplier of two is applied to the base yield; otherwise the multiplier is one. This gives the adjusted yield. If the soil acidity is strictly greater than seven, subtract two units from the adjusted yield due to poor conditions. If the final yield for a location drops below zero, treat it as zero. Return the total mushroom yield summed across all spots. Example: given humidity eighty five, oak count four, and acidity six, the output should be twenty four.

title: Juggling Pattern Tracker
spec: Estimate the total duration of an aerial prop manipulation sequence. Implement `juggle(throws)` where the parameter is a list of lists, each containing a number for throw height, a boolean for hand crossing, and a number for prop weight. The base duration for each action is the throw height multiplied by zero point four. If the hand crossing boolean is true, a crossing penalty of zero point one seconds is added. If the prop weight is greater than five, a weight penalty of zero point two seconds is also added. Add any applicable penalties to the base duration to find the total throw time. Return the cumulative time for the entire sequence. Example: given a sequence with one throw of height three, true for crossing, and weight six, the output should be one point five.

title: Harmonica Tab Translator
spec: Convert a sequence of musical breathing instructions into numerical pitch values. Implement `play(tabs)` where the input is a list of lists, each containing a number for the hole number, a string for the breath direction, and a boolean for whether the slide button is pressed. If the breath direction is draw, the pitch modifier is negative one; if it is blow, the pitch modifier is positive one. The base pitch is calculated by multiplying the hole number by the pitch modifier. If the slide button is pressed, add zero point five to the base pitch to get the final pitch. Return a list of all the final pitch values in order. Example: given hole four, draw direction, and true for the button, the output list should contain negative three point five.

title: Fireworks Display Sequence Scheduler
spec: Write a function `schedule(events)` that processes a list of list values representing planned pyrotechnics. Each sublist contains the burst radius, color intensity, fuse length, and launch altitude. Calculate the optimal launch delay for each by adding the fuse length to the product of launch altitude and burst radius, then subtracting the color intensity. Return a list of calculated delay times in seconds. For example, an input of [[10, 5, 2, 50]] should return [497].

title: Lighthouse Beam Synchronization
spec: Implement `synchronize(towers)` where the input is a list of lists detailing coastal beacons. The inner lists provide the rotation speed, flash duration, bulb intensity, and horizon distance. The synchronization offset is determined by multiplying the horizon distance by the rotation speed, then dividing by the bulb intensity and adding the flash duration. Return a list of the required offset values. An input of [[5, 2, 10, 20]] yields [12].

title: Photography Darkroom Exposure Timer
spec: Create `develop(prints)` to compute the total seconds needed to process photographic prints. The input list contains sublists with the developer chemical strength, stop bath time, fixer duration, paper grade, and light intensity. The processing time for a print is the light intensity divided by the developer chemical strength, plus the stop bath time and the fixer duration, multiplied by the paper grade. Return a list of total seconds for each print. Given [[2, 10, 30, 3, 10]], the output is [135].

title: Watchmaking Gear Train Analyzer
spec: Write `calibrate(gears)` to evaluate a mechanical watch assembly. The input consists of lists holding the mainspring tension, balance wheel oscillation rate, escape wheel teeth count, and friction coefficient. To find the daily drift in seconds, multiply the mainspring tension by the escape wheel teeth count, divide by the balance wheel oscillation rate, and add the friction coefficient. Return the drift values as a list of numbers. For an input of [[15, 5, 20, 2]], the result is [62].

title: Glassblowing Furnace Annealing
spec: Implement `anneal(pieces)` that takes a list of lists specifying glass making parameters. The values provided are the gather size, blowpipe rotation speed, kiln temperature, and crack probability factor. The required cooling duration is calculated by multiplying the gather size by the kiln temperature, dividing by the blowpipe rotation speed, and adding the crack probability factor. Return a list of required cooling durations. Inputting [[5, 10, 800, 20]] yields [420].

title: Tattoo Ink Fading Predictor
spec: Write `predict(sessions)` where the input is a list of sublists representing tattoo applications. The provided metrics are the needle depth, pigment density, sun exposure hours, and skin elasticity. Calculate the expected fading months by multiplying the needle depth and pigment density, then subtracting the product of sun exposure hours and skin elasticity. If the result is less than zero, return zero. Return a list of fading months. For [[3, 50, 10, 2]], the output should be [130].

title: Lockpicking Pin Tumbler Tension
spec: Create `unlock(cylinders)` accepting a list of sublists that detail lock mechanisms. Each entry contains the pin depth, spring resistance, torque pressure, and false set count. The unlock difficulty score is the pin depth added to the spring resistance, multiplied by the torque pressure, with the false set count subtracted from the total. Return a list of these difficulty scores. If the input is [[4, 6, 3, 2]], the output is [28].

title: Shoemaking Leather Stretch Assessor
spec: Implement `stretch(shoes)` to determine how much shoe material will expand. The input list provides sublists containing the leather thickness, moisture content, pulling force, and toe box width. The expansion millimeter value is the pulling force multiplied by the moisture content, divided by the leather thickness, and finally added to the toe box width. Return a list of calculated expansion values. Inputting [[2, 5, 10, 40]] results in [65].

title: Bell Ringing Resonance Tracker
spec: Write `strike(bells)` to evaluate campanology performances based on a list of lists. The given numbers represent the bell weight, rope length, swing angle, and clapper strike force. The total resonance duration in seconds is the bell weight multiplied by the clapper strike force, divided by the rope length, plus the swing angle. Return a list containing the total resonance duration for each bell. For [[500, 10, 45, 2]], the duration output is [145].

title: Papermaking Pulp Drying Estimator
spec: Create `dry(sheets)` to estimate the hours needed to process handmade paper. The input provides lists detailing the fiber length, screen mesh size, pressing pressure, and sheet thickness. The drying hours are calculated by multiplying the fiber length by the sheet thickness, adding the screen mesh size, and dividing the entire sum by the pressing pressure. Return a list of drying hours. Given [[10, 50, 2, 5]], the output is [50].

title: Candle Making Wax Pour Temperature
spec: Implement `melt(batches)` that computes the ideal conditions for candle production. The input is a list of lists holding the wick diameter, wax melting point, fragrance load percentage, and ambient room temperature. The target pour temperature is the wax melting point plus the fragrance load percentage, minus the product of the wick diameter and ambient room temperature. Return a list of target pour temperatures. For an input of [[2, 150, 10, 20]], the result is [120].

title: Soap Making Saponification Timer
spec: Write `cure(molds)` to process lists of artisanal soap properties. The values represent the lye concentration, oil mixture ratio, trace time, and mold insulation factor. The required curing weeks are found by multiplying the oil mixture ratio by the lye concentration, adding the trace time, and then subtracting the mold insulation factor. Return a list of curing weeks. Given [[5, 4, 10, 2]], the expected output is [28].

title: Sausage Casing Stuffing Pressure
spec: Create `stuff(links)` to evaluate the integrity of butcher products. The input list contains sublists with the meat grind size, fat percentage, spice ratio, and casing elasticity. The risk of casing blowout is determined by adding the meat grind size to the fat percentage, multiplying by the spice ratio, and dividing by the casing elasticity. Return a list of blowout risk scores. If the input is [[8, 20, 2, 4]], the output is [14].

title: Taxidermy Hide Preservation Assessor
spec: Implement `preserve(hides)` using a list of lists that contain preparation metrics. The properties are the tanning solution concentration, salt application thickness, stretching tension, and drying humidity. The hide longevity in years is the tanning solution concentration multiplied by the salt application thickness, plus the stretching tension, minus the drying humidity. Return a list of longevity years. For [[10, 3, 15, 40]], the result is [5].

title: Basket Weaving Cane Flexibility
spec: Write `soak(reeds)` to determine the structural limits of weaving materials. The input contains lists specifying the reed thickness, water temperature, soaking hours, and bend radius. The flexibility index is calculated by multiplying the water temperature and soaking hours, dividing by the reed thickness, and adding the bend radius. Return a list of these index values. Given [[4, 20, 2, 10]], the output should be [20].

title: Woodturning Lathe Spindle Speed
spec: Create `turn(blocks)` to find the ideal machinery settings for carving wood. The input provides sublists containing the wood hardness score, lathe revolutions limit, chisel cutting angle, and shaving thickness. The optimal cutting speed is the lathe revolutions limit divided by the wood hardness score, plus the chisel cutting angle multiplied by the shaving thickness. Return a list of optimal speeds. For [[5, 1000, 30, 2]], the result is [260].

title: Stained Glass Soldering Heat
spec: Implement `solder(joints)` to process window assembly parameters given as lists. The inputs are the copper foil width, soldering iron heat, flux amount, and lead tin ratio. Calculate the joint strength score by multiplying the soldering iron heat by the flux amount, dividing by the copper foil width, and adding the lead tin ratio. Return a list of strength scores. Inputting [[5, 400, 2, 60]] gives a score of [220].

title: Neon Sign Gas Luminescence
spec: Write `illuminate(tubes)` handling a list of sublists with electrical and physical properties. The parameters are the tube diameter, electrode voltage, vacuum pressure, and expected brightness level. The stable operation time in hours is calculated by multiplying the electrode voltage by the expected brightness level, dividing by the vacuum pressure, and subtracting the tube diameter. Return a list of operation times. Given [[10, 120, 3, 50]], the output is [1990].

title: Bookbinding Press Curing Time
spec: Create `bind(books)` to determine how long volumes must stay in the finishing press. The list of lists contains the signature page count, thread tension force, adhesive spread thickness, and press clamp pressure. The curing minutes are found by adding the signature page count to the thread tension force, multiplying by the adhesive spread thickness, and dividing by the press clamp pressure. Return a list of curing minutes. For [[100, 20, 5, 10]], the output is [60].

title: Magic Trick Card Sleight Speed
spec: Implement `shuffle(tricks)` to calculate execution metrics for close-up performances. The input is a list of lists holding the deck thickness, palm grip pressure, misdirection duration, and angle of visibility. The deception success rate is the palm grip pressure multiplied by the misdirection duration, divided by the deck thickness, minus the angle of visibility. Return a list of success rates. Inputting [[15, 30, 5, 2]] gives [8].

title: Surfing Wave Catch Momentum
spec: Write `surf(waves)` using a list of sublists to analyze ocean sports conditions. The provided metrics are the swell height, ocean floor depth, board buoyancy rating, and paddling speed. Calculate the wave capture score by adding the swell height and ocean floor depth, multiplying by the paddling speed, and dividing by the board buoyancy rating. Return a list of capture scores. For [[6, 14, 5, 10]], the score is [40].

title: Bungee Jumping Cord Stretch Limit
spec: Create `jump(drops)` to verify safety parameters from a list of sublists. The numbers represent the jumper mass, cord resting length, freefall distance, and maximum rebound height. The cord tension stress is determined by multiplying the jumper mass by the freefall distance, subtracting the cord resting length, and adding the maximum rebound height. Return a list of cord tension stresses. Given [[80, 20, 50, 30]], the output is [4010].

title: Parkour Takeoff Trajectory
spec: Implement `vault(obstacles)` handling a list of lists with athletic movement metrics. The parameters are the approach sprint speed, takeoff launch angle, obstacle clearance distance, and landing absorption flex. The jump efficiency is the approach sprint speed multiplied by the takeoff launch angle, divided by the landing absorption flex, plus the obstacle clearance distance. Return a list of jump efficiencies. For [[15, 45, 10, 5]], the result is [145].

title: Slackline Balance Sway Amplitude
spec: Write `balance(lines)` to evaluate tensioned webbing setups from a list of lists. The inputs provided are the line span length, anchor attachment height, webbing stretch factor, and walker body mass. The sway instability index is the line span length multiplied by the webbing stretch factor, added to the walker body mass, and finally divided by the anchor attachment height. Return a list of instability indices. Inputting [[30, 5, 2, 70]] yields [26].

title: Yo-Yo Sleep Duration Optimizer
spec: Create `throw(tricks)` to estimate the maximum spin time of a toy based on a list of lists. The properties are the string total length, bearing friction coefficient, downward throw velocity, and weight distribution ratio. The expected sleep seconds are found by multiplying the downward throw velocity and weight distribution ratio, subtracting the bearing friction coefficient, and adding the string total length. Return a list of sleep seconds. For an input of [[40, 5, 20, 3]], the output is [95].

title: Orchestral Timpani Pitch Tuning
spec: Write a function `tune(drums)` that processes a list of timpani drum profiles. Each drum has a diameter in inches, a membrane tension level, and a target musical frequency. The logic must calculate the current frequency by multiplying the membrane tension level by ten, then dividing by the diameter. If the current frequency is below the target by more than ten hertz, a tightening adjustment is applied, requiring an adjustment force equal to the frequency difference multiplied by two. Drums that are already within two hertz of the target require zero adjustment, while those with a frequency above the target require loosening, producing a negative adjustment force equal to half the difference. Compute the required adjustment force for each drum and return an array of these adjustment values.

title: Carpet Loom Pattern Density
spec: Implement `weave(sections)` to evaluate parts of an antique rug design. Each section has a thread count per inch, a material stiffness rating, and a dye saturation percentage. Calculate the structural durability score of each section, where the base score is the thread count multiplied by the material stiffness. If the dye saturation exceeds fifty percent, the durability degrades, incurring a penalty equal to the base score multiplied by the excess saturation percentage over fifty. Subtract this penalty to find the final durability. Calculate the average final durability across all sections, and return an array containing only the scores of the sections that have a durability strictly greater than the overall average.

title: Botanical Oil Yield Forecaster
spec: Create a function `distill(batches)` to predict essential oil production. Each batch of plant material has a total weight in kilograms, a moisture content percentage, and an extraction temperature in celsius. First, determine the dry weight of each batch by removing the moisture content from the total weight. The potential oil volume is ten percent of the dry weight. The actual oil yield is reduced if the extraction temperature deviates from the ideal ninety degrees celsius, losing five percent of the potential volume for every degree above or below ninety. Calculate and return the total actual oil yield across all batches, strictly ignoring any batch where the calculated actual yield drops below zero.

title: Dancing Water Fountain Synchronizer
spec: Develop `choreograph(nozzles)` to plan a fountain show sequence. Each nozzle object has a maximum water pressure, a current angle in degrees, and a target height in meters. Calculate the required pressure pulse to reach the target height, which is the target height multiplied by a gravity constant of nine point eight, all divided by the cosine of the current angle. If the required pressure pulse exceeds the maximum water pressure of the nozzle, the nozzle cannot reach the target, so it must lower its target height by twenty percent and recalculate the required pressure pulse. Return an array containing the final safe pressure pulse values for all nozzles in the sequence.

title: Sushi Rice Seasoning Saturation
spec: Write `marinate(batches)` to evaluate the preparation of seasoned rice. Each batch of rice provides a volume in cups, a resting time in minutes, and a temperature in celsius. Calculate a base saturation index for each batch by multiplying the volume by a standard absorption rate of zero point fifteen. Ideal vinegar absorption requires a resting time of at least thirty minutes and a temperature below forty degrees. Decrease the saturation index by two percent for every minute the resting time is under thirty, and reduce it further by five percent for every degree the temperature is over forty. Return the maximum final saturation index found among all the prepared batches.

title: Tobacco Leaf Fermentation Humidity
spec: Implement `cure(leaves)` to track the moisture loss in curing barns. Each leaf pile provides an initial moisture level, an ambient humidity percentage, and a fermentation duration in days. The curing process removes moisture daily. The daily moisture reduction is the difference between the initial moisture and the ambient humidity, multiplied by a standard drying factor of zero point zero four. However, if the ambient humidity is above seventy percent, the curing slows down, dropping the drying factor to zero point zero two. Calculate the final moisture level for each leaf pile after the specified duration days have passed. Return an array of the final moisture levels.

title: Cathedral Organ Wind Pressure
spec: Create `regulate(pipes)` to determine the airflow required for a chord. Each organ pipe provides a length in meters, a diameter in centimeters, and a boolean indicating if it requires high sound intensity. Calculate the base air volume needed by multiplying the length by the square of the diameter. To achieve the proper tone, the base air volume is multiplied by an acoustic factor, which is one point five if high sound intensity is required, and one point two otherwise. Long pipes measuring over three meters require an additional ten percent volume to overcome air resistance. Sum all the final required air volumes and return the total wind pressure demand as a single number.

title: Marionette Rigging Stress
spec: Develop `balance(puppets)` to assess the physical strain on puppet controllers. Each puppet limb provides a physical weight, a suspension string length, and a movement speed factor. The dynamic rigging stress on each string is calculated by multiplying the physical weight by the movement speed factor. Longer strings introduce a wobble penalty, adding a stress multiplier of one point one for every ten units of string length over fifty. Apply this multiplier to the dynamic rigging stress to find the final tension load. If the final tension load exceeds a critical threshold of two hundred, the string is marked for reinforcement. Return the total count of strings requiring reinforcement.

title: Hedge Maze Complexity Scorer
spec: Write `navigate(paths)` to evaluate the difficulty of finding the center of a labyrinth. Each maze path specifies a segment length, a count of dead ends, and a twistiness rating. The base navigation difficulty is the segment length multiplied by the twistiness rating. Each dead end adds fifty points to the difficulty. If a path has more than five dead ends, it triggers a frustration multiplier, increasing the total calculated difficulty by twenty five percent. Return an array containing the final difficulties of the paths, sorted from highest to lowest.

title: Kaleidoscope Prism Angles
spec: Implement `reflect(mirrors)` to calculate the visual brilliance of an optical toy. Each mirror segment provides an incident angle, a glass clarity score, and a light source intensity. The raw reflection power is the light source intensity multiplied by the glass clarity score. The effective visual output is determined by adjusting the raw reflection power based on the incident angle. Angles between forty five and sixty degrees maximize the reflection, retaining the full raw power. Angles outside this optimal range cause light scattering, which reduces the raw reflection power by thirty percent. Return the average effective visual output across all provided mirror segments.

title: Obelisk Shadow Time Projection
spec: Create `project(shadows)` to estimate historical timekeeping data. Each shadow measurement provides a length in meters, an azimuth angle, and a boolean indicating if it was recorded in summer. The base estimated solar hour is derived by dividing the length by the cosine of the azimuth angle. During summer, the estimated solar hour is adjusted backwards by one point five hours due to changes in the solar zenith, while winter measurements are adjusted forward by one hour. Calculate the final estimated solar hour for each measurement, ensuring no hour falls below zero or exceeds twenty four, and return an array of these times.

title: Ceramic Kiln Shrinkage Profiler
spec: Develop `fire(sculptures)` to predict the final dimensions of clay art. Each sculpture provides a wet clay volume, a water content percentage, and a firing temperature. The expected moisture loss is the wet clay volume multiplied by the water content percentage. The thermal contraction is calculated by taking two percent of the remaining solid volume for every hundred degrees the firing temperature exceeds one thousand degrees. Calculate the final fired volume by subtracting both the expected moisture loss and the thermal contraction from the initial wet clay volume. Return an array containing the final fired volume of each sculpture.

title: Wooden Boomerang Return Arc
spec: Write `throw(boomerangs)` to simulate aerodynamic sports equipment. Each boomerang throw provides an initial throw velocity, a wind resistance factor, and an airfoil curvature rating. The initial flight distance is the initial throw velocity squared, divided by ten. The wind resistance factor shortens this flight distance by five percent per unit of resistance. The return trajectory accuracy depends on the airfoil curvature rating. Curvature ratings below seven cause a complete return failure, overriding the return distance to zero. Otherwise, the return distance matches the shortened flight distance. Calculate and return an array of the final return distances.

title: Pogo Stick Recoil Dynamics
spec: Implement `bounce(springs)` to test recreational jumping devices. Each spring configuration provides a coil thickness, a rider mass, and a compression depth. The stored kinetic energy is calculated by multiplying the compression depth by a spring constant, which is simply the coil thickness squared. The raw upward recoil velocity is the square root of the stored kinetic energy divided by the rider mass. If the raw upward recoil velocity exceeds a safe limit of fifteen, a dampening mechanism engages, reducing the velocity by twenty percent to yield the final recoil velocity. Return the maximum final recoil velocity found among all configurations.

title: Hula Hoop Gyroscopic Stability
spec: Create `spin(hoops)` to analyze the physical forces required to keep a hoop aloft. Each hoop action provides a hoop radius, a rotational velocity, and a body friction coefficient. The outward centrifugal force is the square of the rotational velocity multiplied by the hoop radius. The base stability index is the outward centrifugal force divided by the body friction coefficient. If the rotational velocity ever drops below a minimum threshold of five, the stability index immediately becomes zero, indicating the hoop falls to the ground. Calculate the final stability index for each action and return a total count of how many actions resulted in a stability index greater than fifty.

title: Jump Rope Arc Clearance
spec: Develop `swing(ropes)` to evaluate playground clearance heights. Each rope swing provides a total rope length, a hand spread distance, and a swing speed in rotations per minute. The base vertical arc clearance is estimated by subtracting the hand spread distance from the total rope length, then multiplying by a rope sag factor. The standard rope sag factor is zero point eight, but high swing speeds above one hundred rotations per minute tighten the arc considerably, increasing the sag factor to zero point nine five. Calculate the vertical arc clearance for each swing and return an array containing only the clearances that are strictly greater than two meters.

title: Didgeridoo Soundwave Amplification
spec: Write `resonate(tubes)` to calculate the acoustics of wooden wind instruments. Each tube provides an inner diameter, a total length, and a wood density value. The base acoustic resonance frequency is derived by dividing a sound speed constant of three hundred forty by twice the total length. The amplification multiplier depends on the inner diameter and wood density. High density wood over eight hundred increases the amplification multiplier by fifteen percent, while a large inner diameter over five centimeters reduces it by ten percent. Apply the multiplier to the base acoustic resonance frequency and return an array of the final calculated amplification values.

title: Arcade Pinball Flipper Velocity
spec: Implement `flip(targets)` to model the mechanics of an amusement machine. Each flipper activation provides a solenoid power level, a metal ball weight, and an upward incline angle. The raw strike force is the solenoid power level divided by the metal ball weight. The effective upward velocity is the raw strike force minus a table gravity penalty, which is proportional to the sine of the upward incline angle multiplied by ten. If the effective upward velocity evaluates to a negative number, the ball is not propelled forward at all, and the velocity is safely capped at zero. Calculate the effective upward velocity for each activation and return the sum of all velocities.

title: Apple Cider Pressing Yield Estimator
spec: The function `estimate(orchard)` receives a list of apple batches. Each batch is an object containing the apple variety name, the total weight in pounds, the average juice content percentage, and the press efficiency factor. Calculate the extracted juice volume for each batch by multiplying the total weight by the juice content percentage and then by the press efficiency factor. If the variety is a heritage breed, add a ten percent bonus to the extracted juice. Return a list of numbers representing the final juice volume for each batch, rounded to two decimal places. Example: input with a single batch of variety Gala, total weight one hundred, average juice content percentage zero point six, and press efficiency factor zero point eight returns forty-eight.

title: Ostrich Egg Incubation Tracker
spec: The function `track(nests)` processes a list of ostrich nests. Each nest provides the ambient temperature, the relative humidity, the egg turning frequency per day, and the current days incubated. Calculate the hatch probability score for each nest. Start with a base score of fifty. Add two points for every day incubated over thirty. If the ambient temperature is between thirty-five and thirty-seven, add twenty points. If the relative humidity is exactly twenty-five percent, add fifteen points, otherwise subtract five points. Multiply the score by the turning frequency divided by four, capped at a maximum multiplier of one. Return a list of boolean values, true if the final score is over eighty, false otherwise. Example: nest with ambient temperature thirty-six, relative humidity twenty-five, egg turning frequency four, and current days incubated thirty-two returns true.

title: Bespoke Suit Fabric Estimator
spec: The function `measure(clients)` receives a list of client measurements. Each client object has a shoulder width, a torso length, an arm length, and an inseam measurement in centimeters. Calculate the total fabric required for each client. The jacket fabric is the torso length plus the arm length, multiplied by the shoulder width, divided by fifty. The trousers fabric is the inseam measurement multiplied by two point five. Add both values together. If the client requested a three piece suit, indicated by a boolean flag for vest included, add an extra one hundred and fifty centimeters. Convert the final total from centimeters to meters by dividing by one hundred. Return a list of fabric lengths in meters. Example: shoulder width fifty, torso length sixty, arm length sixty, inseam measurement eighty, and vest included true returns four point seven meters.

title: Vanilla Bean Curing Timer
spec: The function `time(beans)` accepts a list of vanilla bean batches. Each batch provides the initial moisture percentage, the pod length in centimeters, the sweating box temperature, and the daily sun exposure in hours. Calculate the required curing time in days. Subtract thirty from the initial moisture percentage, then multiply by two. Add the pod length multiplied by zero point five. Subtract the daily sun exposure multiplied by one point five. If the sweating box temperature is above forty degrees, reduce the total curing time by five days. Return a list of curing times rounded to the nearest integer. Example: initial moisture percentage sixty, pod length fifteen, sweating box temperature forty-two, and daily sun exposure four returns fifty-seven days.

title: Diamond Rough Cut Analyzer
spec: The function `analyze(stones)` evaluates a list of rough diamonds. Each stone is described by its carat weight, its primary inclusion depth in millimeters, its refractive index, and a boolean indicating if it has internal fractures. Calculate the maximum theoretical yield percentage. Start with a base yield of sixty percent. Subtract five percent if the primary inclusion depth is greater than two millimeters. If the refractive index is above two point four, add ten percent to the yield. If the stone has internal fractures, multiply the entire current yield by zero point five. Return a list of the final yield percentages for each stone. If any calculated yield is below twenty, return zero for that stone. Example: carat weight two, primary inclusion depth one, refractive index two point five, and internal fractures false returns seventy percent.

title: Silkworm Cocoon Thread Yield
spec: The function `harvest(trays)` accepts a list of rearing trays. Each tray has the number of mature worms, the average cocoon weight in grams, the silk quality grade, and the days since spinning started. Calculate the total silk thread length in meters for each tray. Multiply the number of mature worms by the average cocoon weight to get the total cocoon mass. Multiply the mass by a quality multiplier: one thousand for grade A, eight hundred for grade B, and five hundred for grade C. If the days since spinning started is less than eight, the harvest is premature, so deduct twenty percent from the thread length. Return a list of the final lengths. Example: fifty mature worms, average cocoon weight two, silk quality grade A, and ten days since spinning started returns one hundred thousand meters.

title: Alpaca Fleece Shearing Estimator
spec: The function `shear(herd)` processes a list of alpacas. Each provides the age in years, the time since last shearing in months, the fleece density score, and the animal weight in kilograms. Calculate the expected fleece yield in grams for each alpaca. Multiply the animal weight by the fleece density score, then multiply by fifty. If the time since last shearing is greater than twelve months, add ten percent to the yield. If the age in years is greater than ten, reduce the yield by fifteen percent due to age related thinning. Return a list of expected yields rounded to the nearest integer. Example: age five, time since last shearing fourteen, fleece density score three, and animal weight sixty returns nine thousand nine hundred grams.

title: Chameleon Camouflage Transition Delay
spec: The function `predict(reptiles)` evaluates a list of chameleons. Each provides the starting skin luminance, the target background hue score, the ambient temperature, and the animal stress level. Calculate the transition delay in seconds. Find the absolute value of the target background hue score minus the starting skin luminance, then multiply this difference by zero point five. If the ambient temperature is below twenty degrees, add ten seconds because cold slows the physical reaction. Add the animal stress level multiplied by two. Return an array of the transition delays. Example: starting skin luminance fifty, target background hue score eighty, ambient temperature eighteen, and animal stress level three returns thirty-one seconds.

title: Truffle Hound Search Stamina
spec: The function `evaluate(dogs)` evaluates a list of hunting dogs. Each dog has its current energy level out of one hundred, the terrain difficulty score from one to ten, the ambient temperature, and the number of truffles found so far. Calculate the remaining search time in minutes. Multiply the current energy level by three. Subtract the terrain difficulty score multiplied by five. If the ambient temperature is above twenty-five, subtract an additional twenty minutes due to heat exhaustion. Add ten minutes for every truffle found so far, representing an excitement boost. If the result is negative, return zero. Return a list of remaining search times. Example: current energy level fifty, terrain difficulty score five, ambient temperature thirty, and three truffles found returns one hundred and thirty-five minutes.

title: Falcon Stoop Velocity Predictor
spec: The function `predict(flights)` processes a list of falcon flights. Each flight details the starting altitude in meters, the bird weight in grams, the wind resistance factor, and the angle of descent in degrees. Calculate the expected terminal velocity of the dive. Multiply the starting altitude by zero point five. Add the bird weight divided by ten. Subtract the wind resistance factor multiplied by two. If the angle of descent is exactly ninety degrees, add twenty to the final speed representing a perfect vertical stoop. Return a list of calculated velocities. Example: starting altitude one thousand, bird weight one thousand, wind resistance five, and angle of descent ninety returns six hundred and ten.

title: Fountain Pen Ink Bleed Assessor
spec: The function `assess(inks)` evaluates a list of ink samples on paper. Each sample has the ink viscosity score, the nib width in millimeters, the paper weight in grams per square meter, and a boolean for paper coating. Calculate the bleed-through severity index. Multiply the nib width by ten. Divide the result by the ink viscosity score. Subtract the paper weight divided by fifty. If the paper coating is true, reduce the severity index by two. If the index is less than zero, return zero. Return an array of the calculated indices. Example: ink viscosity two, nib width one point five, paper weight one hundred, and paper coating false returns five point five.

title: Geyser Eruption Interval Forecaster
spec: The function `forecast(geysers)` takes a list of geyser observations. Each observation has the previous eruption duration in minutes, the underground chamber volume, the geothermal heat index, and the current water inflow rate. Estimate the time in minutes until the next eruption. Multiply the previous eruption duration by four. Add the underground chamber volume divided by the current water inflow rate. Subtract the geothermal heat index multiplied by two. If the calculated interval is less than thirty minutes, set it to thirty minutes as a minimum recharge period. Return a list of estimated intervals. Example: previous eruption duration ten, underground chamber volume five hundred, current water inflow rate ten, and geothermal heat index five returns eighty minutes.

title: Peat Bog Carbon Sequestration
spec: The function `estimate(bogs)` processes a list of peat bog regions. Each region includes the surface area in hectares, the average peat depth in meters, the annual rainfall in millimeters, and a boolean flag for active restoration. Calculate the tons of carbon sequestered per year. Multiply the surface area by the average peat depth, then multiply by a base sequestration rate of three point five. If the annual rainfall is above one thousand millimeters, multiply the calculated sequestration by one point one five. If active restoration is true, add a flat bonus of fifty tons. Return an array of the calculated carbon tons. Example: surface area ten, average peat depth two, annual rainfall one thousand two hundred, and active restoration true returns one hundred and thirty point five tons.

title: Desert Sand Dune Migration Rate
spec: The function `calculate(dunes)` accepts a list of sand dunes. Each dune is described by its crest height in meters, the average wind speed in kilometers per hour, the sand grain size in millimeters, and the vegetation cover percentage. Determine the annual migration distance in meters. Square the average wind speed and divide by the crest height. If the sand grain size is less than zero point five, multiply the distance by one point three because fine sand moves faster. Subtract the vegetation cover percentage multiplied by zero point two. If the resulting distance is less than zero, return zero. Return the list of migration distances. Example: crest height ten, average wind speed twenty, sand grain size zero point four, and vegetation cover percentage ten returns fifty meters.

title: Cathedral Gargoyle Erosion Tracker
spec: The function `track(gargoyles)` processes a list of stone gargoyles. Each gargoyle details the original carving depth in centimeters, the century carved, the local acid rain index, and the prevailing wind speed in knots. Calculate the current carving depth. Subtract the century carved from twenty-one to get the age in centuries. Multiply the age by the local acid rain index, then multiply by zero point five. Add the prevailing wind speed multiplied by zero point one. Subtract this total erosion amount from the original carving depth. If the result is negative, return zero. Return a list of the current depths. Example: original carving depth ten, century carved nineteen, local acid rain index four, and prevailing wind speed twenty returns four.

title: Mangrove Salt Filtration Capacity
spec: The function `measure(trees)` takes a list of mangrove trees. Each tree specifies the root surface area, the surrounding water salinity, the tree age in years, and the tide flush frequency. Calculate the grams of salt filtered per day. Multiply the root surface area by the surrounding water salinity, then divide by ten. If the tree age is greater than twenty, add fifteen percent to the capacity due to developed root systems. Multiply the result by the tide flush frequency divided by two. Return a list of the filtered salt amounts. Example: root surface area five, surrounding water salinity thirty, tree age twenty-five, and tide flush frequency four returns thirty-four point five grams.

title: Cave Stalactite Drip Rate
spec: The function `analyze(formations)` receives a list of stalactite formations. Each formation has the surface drip pool volume, the limestone porosity score, the cave humidity percentage, and the seasonal rainfall in millimeters. Predict the drip rate in drops per minute. Multiply the surface drip pool volume by the limestone porosity score. Add the seasonal rainfall divided by ten. If the cave humidity percentage is above ninety, subtract five drops per minute because less evaporation occurs. If the final drip rate exceeds one hundred, cap it at one hundred. Return the array of calculated drip rates. Example: surface drip pool volume ten, limestone porosity score five, cave humidity percentage ninety-five, and seasonal rainfall two hundred returns sixty-five drops per minute.

title: Arctic Permafrost Thaw Depth
spec: The function `evaluate(regions)` processes a list of permafrost regions. Each region includes the summer temperature average, the days above freezing, the snow cover thickness in winter, and the soil organic matter percentage. Calculate the active thaw depth in centimeters. Multiply the summer temperature average by the days above freezing, then divide by fifty. Subtract the snow cover thickness because it acts as insulation against spring heat. Add the soil organic matter percentage multiplied by two. If the thaw depth is negative, return zero. Return a list of the active thaw depths. Example: summer temperature average ten, days above freezing one hundred, snow cover thickness ten, and soil organic matter percentage five returns twenty centimeters.

title: Canopy Sunlight Penetration
spec: The function `assess(plots)` accepts a list of forest plots. Each plot provides the upper canopy density percentage, the mid layer leaf area index, the sun angle in degrees, and the cloud cover percentage. Calculate the sunlight intensity reaching the forest floor as a percentage. Start with one hundred percent. Reduce it by the upper canopy density percentage. Then subtract the mid layer leaf area index multiplied by five. Multiply the remaining percentage by the sine of the sun angle converted to radians. Finally, reduce the result by the cloud cover percentage divided by two. If the final value is below zero, return zero. Return the list of sunlight intensities. Example: upper canopy density percentage forty, mid layer leaf area index four, sun angle ninety, and cloud cover percentage twenty returns thirty percent.

title: Bamboo Stalk Daily Growth
spec: The function `track(stalks)` takes a list of bamboo stalks. Each stalk contains the current stalk height in centimeters, the soil nitrogen level, the daily rainfall in millimeters, and the sunlight exposure in hours. Calculate the daily growth in centimeters. Multiply the soil nitrogen level by the daily rainfall, then divide by twenty. Add the sunlight exposure multiplied by one point five. If the current stalk height is greater than one thousand centimeters, halve the daily growth rate since older stalks grow slower. Return an array of daily growth values. Example: current stalk height five hundred, soil nitrogen level forty, daily rainfall ten, and sunlight exposure ten returns thirty-five centimeters.

title: Venus Flytrap Digestion Timer
spec: The function `estimate(traps)` evaluates a list of flytraps. Each trap specifies the insect mass in grams, the trap size in centimeters, the ambient temperature, and the digestive enzyme concentration. Calculate the digestion time in hours. Multiply the insect mass by fifty. Divide the result by the trap size. Subtract the ambient temperature multiplied by one point two. Divide the remaining time by the digestive enzyme concentration. If the calculated time is less than twenty-four hours, enforce a minimum digestion time of twenty-four hours. Return a list of digestion times. Example: insect mass five, trap size five, ambient temperature twenty, and digestive enzyme concentration one returns twenty-six hours.

title: Sloth Metabolic Energy Tracker
spec: The function `calculate(sloths)` receives a list of sloths. Each sloth has its body mass in kilograms, the hours slept today, the leaves consumed in grams, and the average heart rate. Determine the net energy balance in calories. Multiply the leaves consumed by two to get the caloric intake. Calculate the resting energy burned by multiplying the body mass by the hours slept, then multiplying by five. Calculate the active energy burned by subtracting the hours slept from twenty-four, multiplying by the average heart rate, and dividing by two. The net balance is the caloric intake minus both burned amounts. Return a list of net energy balances. Example: body mass five, hours slept fifteen, leaves consumed five hundred, and average heart rate forty returns four hundred and forty-five calories.

title: Camel Hump Hydration Storage
spec: The function `forecast(camels)` processes a list of camels. Each camel contains the hump volume in liters, the days since last drink, the desert ambient temperature, and the daily travel distance in kilometers. Calculate the remaining hydration percentage. Start with one hundred percent. Subtract two percent for every day since the last drink. If the desert ambient temperature is above forty degrees, subtract an additional one percent per day. Subtract the daily travel distance multiplied by zero point five. If the hump volume is less than twenty liters, subtract an extra ten percent flat penalty. Return an array of remaining hydration percentages capped at zero minimum. Example: hump volume thirty, days since last drink five, desert ambient temperature forty-five, and daily travel distance twenty returns seventy-five percent.

title: Electric Eel Voltage Discharge
spec: The function `measure(eels)` takes a list of electric eels. Each eel specifies the body length in meters, the water salinity level, the threat proximity in centimeters, and the recent feeding status as a boolean. Calculate the discharge voltage. Multiply the body length by two hundred. If the water salinity level is less than five, multiply the voltage by zero point eight due to poor conductivity. If the threat proximity is less than fifty centimeters, add one hundred volts to the discharge. If the recent feeding status is false, reduce the final voltage by fifty. Return a list of the calculated voltages. Example: body length two, water salinity level ten, threat proximity forty, and recent feeding status true returns five hundred volts.

title: Platypus Venom Toxicity Level
spec: The function `evaluate(animals)` accepts a list of platypuses. Each animal provides the spur length in millimeters, the mating season status as a boolean, the animal age in years, and the overall health score out of ten. Calculate the venom toxicity index. Multiply the spur length by the overall health score. If the mating season status is true, double the index. If the animal age is greater than ten, subtract twenty from the index as older animals produce weaker venom. If the index falls below zero, set it to zero. Return an array of the toxicity indices for all the animals. Example: spur length fifteen, mating season status true, animal age five, and overall health score eight returns two hundred and forty.

title: Monorail Track Wear Assessor
spec: Write a function `assess(segments)` that calculates the deterioration of a transit system. The input is a list of track segments, where each segment is a list containing the segment length in kilometers, the usage hours, and a friction coefficient. The base track wear is calculated by multiplying the segment length by the usage hours. Adjust this base wear upwards by twenty percent if the friction coefficient is strictly greater than zero point eight. Sum these adjusted track wear values for the entire system and return a single total system wear number. Example: [[10, 100, 0.5], [5, 200, 0.9]] yields 2200.

title: Hologram Voxel Resolution Scaler
spec: Implement `scale(voxels)` to adjust a 3D projection. The input is a list of data points, where each point is a list of three numbers representing horizontal position, vertical position, and light intensity. Filter out any points where the light intensity is below forty. For the remaining valid points, multiply both the horizontal position and the vertical position by a scaling factor of two point five to enlarge the projection. Return a list of lists containing the new horizontal position, the new vertical position, and the original light intensity for each valid point. Example: [[10, 20, 50], [5, 5, 10]] yields [[25, 50, 50]].

title: Prosthetic Nerve Signal Processor
spec: Create a function `process(signals)` to interpret neural commands for a robotic limb. The input is a list of incoming pulses, where each is a list containing the pulse amplitude, the pulse duration in milliseconds, and a target muscle index. Ignore any pulses with a pulse amplitude under ten, as they are background noise. For valid pulses, calculate the total activation energy by multiplying the pulse amplitude by the pulse duration. Group the total activation energy by the target muscle index, summing the energies for each index. Return a list of the accumulated total activation energies, ordered by the target muscle index from zero upwards. Example: [[12, 5, 0], [8, 10, 1], [15, 2, 0]] yields [90].

title: Trebuchet Range Calculator
spec: Write `target(parameters)` to determine the firing distance of a medieval siege weapon. The input is a single list containing counterweight mass, projectile mass, sling length, and pivot height. The theoretical maximum range is calculated by multiplying the counterweight mass by the pivot height, dividing that product by the projectile mass, and then adding twice the sling length. If the projectile mass is over fifty, reduce the theoretical maximum range by fifteen percent to account for heavy payload air resistance. Return the final calculated range rounded to the nearest integer. Example: [1000, 40, 5, 10] yields 260.

title: Maglev Electromagnetic Propulsion Monitor
spec: Develop a function `propel(coils)` to verify the launch sequence of a levitating train. The input is a list of track coils, each represented as a list containing the base magnetic flux, current electrical draw, and a thermal sensor reading in Celsius. The effective propulsion force of a coil is its base magnetic flux multiplied by its current electrical draw. However, if the thermal sensor reading exceeds eighty degrees, the effective propulsion force is reduced by fifty percent due to thermal throttling. Calculate the total propulsion force across all coils and return true if this total force exceeds a minimum launch threshold of ten thousand, otherwise return false. Example: [[500, 10, 70], [400, 15, 90]] yields false.

title: Biodigester Methane Yield Estimator
spec: Implement `estimate(batches)` to forecast energy production from organic waste. The input is a list of waste batches, each provided as a list containing wet mass in kilograms, dry matter percentage (as a decimal), and the carbon to nitrogen ratio. First, calculate the dry mass by multiplying the wet mass by the dry matter percentage. The base methane yield is the dry mass multiplied by zero point four. If the carbon to nitrogen ratio is between twenty and thirty inclusive, it represents optimal conditions, so increase the batch methane yield by twenty five percent. Return the sum of all final batch yields rounded down to the nearest integer. Example: [[100, 0.20, 25], [50, 0.40, 10]] yields 18.

title: Exoplanet Atmosphere Spectral Analyzer
spec: Create `analyze(spectra)` to process telescope data for alien atmospheres. The input is a list of light spectrum bands, each given as a list containing a baseline emission wavelength, an observed wavelength, and an absorption depth. Determine the spectral wavelength shift by subtracting the baseline emission wavelength from the observed wavelength. Calculate a signature confidence rating by multiplying the spectral wavelength shift by the absorption depth. If the signature confidence rating is above zero point one, the band is classified as a confirmed heavy gas signature. Return the total count of confirmed heavy gas signatures found in the data. Example: [[500, 502, 0.08], [400, 399, 0.1], [600, 605, 0.02]] yields 1.

title: Tidal Barrage Energy Predictor
spec: Write a function `predict(tides)` to calculate power generation from an ocean bay. The input is a list of daily tide cycles, each formatted as a list with the high tide height in meters, the low tide height in meters, and the basin holding capacity in cubic meters. Calculate the daily tidal range by subtracting the low tide height from the high tide height. The base generated energy is the daily tidal range multiplied by the basin holding capacity, then multiplied by a turbine efficiency factor of zero point eight. If the daily tidal range is strictly less than two meters, the turbines cannot spin, so the generated energy for that cycle is exactly zero. Return a list of the generated energy values for each consecutive day. Example: [[5, 1, 1000], [2.5, 1, 1000]] yields [3200, 0].

title: Autonomous Snowcat Grooming Router
spec: Develop `groom(sectors)` to plan the path for a robot clearing ski slopes. The input is a list of mountain sectors, each represented as a list containing the sector path length in meters, the average snow depth in centimeters, and a terrain steepness percentage. The base grooming time for a sector is its sector path length divided by a standard operational speed of one hundred meters per minute. If the terrain steepness percentage exceeds thirty, multiply the base grooming time by one point five to account for cautious driving. Furthermore, if the average snow depth is below twenty centimeters, the sector must be skipped to avoid damaging the tracks, taking zero time. Return the total grooming time required for all valid sectors. Example: [[500, 30, 40], [200, 15, 10], [300, 40, 20]] yields 10.5.

title: Spider Silk Tensile Tester
spec: Implement `test(strands)` to evaluate biological materials for a laboratory. The input is a list of tested silk strands, each provided as a list of maximum stretch length, thread microscopic thickness, and ambient testing humidity percentage. The base structural strength score is determined by dividing the maximum stretch length by the thread microscopic thickness. High moisture severely weakens the proteins, so if the ambient testing humidity percentage is strictly above sixty, reduce the base structural strength score by a third to produce the final strength score. Calculate the final strength score for each strand and return the arithmetic average of all final strength scores. Example: [[100, 2, 50], [120, 3, 75]] yields 38.33333333333333.

title: Cybernetic Retina Pixel Translator
spec: Write a function `translate(photons)` to route visual data in a bionic eye. The input is a list of detected light events, each represented as a list of incident photon wavelength, total photon count, and retinal sector index. For each event, classify the color channel: wavelengths from four hundred to just under five hundred are blue, five hundred to just under six hundred are green, and six hundred to just under seven hundred are red. Ignore all other wavelengths. Multiply the total photon count by a signal amplification factor of one point two for blue, one point five for green, and one point zero for red to get the final channel intensity. Return a list of three numbers representing the accumulated intensities for the blue, green, and red channels respectively. Example: [[450, 100, 1], [550, 200, 2], [750, 50, 1]] yields [120, 300, 0].

title: Choral Harmony Evaluator
spec: Create `harmonize(voices)` to analyze a choir's acoustic blend. The input is a list of sung notes, each a list containing a fundamental frequency, an overtone amplitude, and a vibrato variation metric. First, calculate a pitch stability score for each note by dividing the fundamental frequency by the vibrato variation metric. Then, calculate a harmonic blend metric by multiplying the overtone amplitude by the pitch stability score. A note is considered perfectly blended if its pitch stability score is above fifty and its harmonic blend metric is strictly less than fifteen. Return a list containing two values: the total count of perfectly blended notes, followed by the sum of the pitch stability scores across all evaluated notes. Example: [[440, 0.2, 5], [880, 0.4, 20]] yields [1, 132].

title: Fungal Mycelium Network Router
spec: Develop `route(nodes)` to simulate organic resource distribution. The input is a list of environmental nutrient deposits, each described as a list containing the absolute distance from the central spore, the available sugar concentration, and the local mineral density. A deposit is classified as a viable expansion target if its available sugar concentration is strictly greater than its absolute distance from the central spore. For all viable expansion targets, calculate a network growth priority by multiplying the available sugar concentration by the local mineral density, and then dividing that product by the absolute distance. Return the maximum network growth priority among all viable targets, or return zero if none are viable. Example: [[5, 10, 2], [20, 15, 3]] yields 4.

title: Medieval Siege Battering Ram Momentum
spec: Implement `breach(strikes)` to assess structural damage to a castle gate. The input is a list of ram swings, each a list containing the tree log mass, the maximum swing velocity, and the final impact angle in degrees. The base impact force is the tree log mass multiplied by the square of the maximum swing velocity. Adjust this force for the glancing nature of the blow by using a simplified angle multiplier, calculated as one minus the final impact angle divided by ninety. Multiply the base impact force by this simplified angle multiplier to get the true structural damage for the swing. Sum the true structural damage of all recorded strikes and return the grand total. Example: [[500, 4, 0], [500, 4, 45]] yields 12000.

title: Deep Sea Sonar Mapper
spec: Write a function `map(echoes)` to process underwater topography readings. The input is a list of sound returns, each a list with the acoustic ping travel time in seconds, the echo return frequency in kilohertz, and the acoustic scattering intensity. The estimated ocean depth is calculated by multiplying the acoustic ping travel time by the speed of sound in water, which is a constant one thousand five hundred meters per second, and then dividing the result by two. If the echo return frequency deviates from the standard emission frequency of fifty kilohertz by more than ten percent, the return is considered biological noise and must be ignored entirely. Collect the estimated ocean depths for all valid returns and return their overall average. Example: [[2, 50, 0.8], [4, 60, 0.5]] yields 1500.

title: Oyster Bed Filtration Modeler
spec: Create `model(beds)` to estimate water quality improvement in an estuary. The input is a list of oyster colonies, each a list containing the current living oyster count, the ambient water turbidity level, and the average daily water temperature in Celsius. The base daily filtration volume in liters is calculated by multiplying the current living oyster count by a constant base filtration rate of fifty. If the ambient water turbidity level exceeds a threshold of four hundred, the oysters suffer from gill clogging and filter twenty percent less water. Furthermore, if the average daily water temperature drops below ten degrees, they enter hibernation and filter absolutely zero water. Return a list of the final daily filtration volumes for each evaluated colony. Example: [[100, 300, 15], [100, 500, 12], [100, 300, 8]] yields [5000, 4000, 0].

title: Steampunk Airship Buoyancy Balancer
spec: Develop `balance(chambers)` to calculate the net lift of a dirigible. The input is a list of internal gas envelopes, each a list containing the envelope volumetric capacity in cubic meters, the current internal gas pressure, and a release valve status integer where one means open and zero means closed. The gross lift generated by a chamber is calculated by multiplying its envelope volumetric capacity by its current internal gas pressure. However, if a chamber has an open release valve status, its pressure is effectively neutralized, meaning its gross lift becomes zero for the overall calculation. Sum the gross lift of all chambers and subtract a fixed heavy gondola weight of five thousand. Return the total net buoyancy force. Example: [[2000, 3, 0], [1000, 2, 1]] yields 1000.

title: Nuclear Reactor Core Moderation Assessor
spec: Implement `assess(rods)` to evaluate the safety status of a power plant. The input is a list of mechanical control rods, each given as a list containing the current insertion depth in centimeters, the baseline neutron absorption cross section, and the surrounding primary coolant temperature in Celsius. The effective moderation factor for a rod is calculated by multiplying its current insertion depth by its baseline neutron absorption cross section. However, if the surrounding primary coolant temperature exceeds three hundred degrees, the effective moderation factor is reduced by fifteen percent due to physical thermal expansion of the graphite lattice. Sum the effective moderation factors across all rods to find the total core moderation value. If this total core moderation value is strictly less than five thousand, return false to trigger an immediate emergency scram; otherwise, return true. Example: [[100, 20, 250], [100, 20, 350]] yields false.
